# User Stories

Every story serves one job from the jobs document. A story is Implemented only when every one of its criteria has passed. Otherwise it is Not implemented, and a note names the criteria that have no evidence yet.

How to read the criteria:
- Bill, Tip % and People are the three entries. The page opens with Bill empty, Tip % showing 15 and People showing 2.
- Bill and Tip % take at least one digit and at most one decimal point. People takes digits only. Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces around an entry are ignored.
- The result has the tip amount (labelled Tip), the total (labelled Total, the bill plus the tip) and Each person pays, a numbered list with one amount per person. When the total does not divide evenly, a note about the extra cents appears in the result.
- Amounts have two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.
- Messages are quoted exactly as the page shows them. In a criterion about one entry, the other two entries are valid, so only that entry shows a message.

## S-1 (serves J-1, Not implemented): See what everyone owes

As a Table Payer, I want to enter the bill, the tip and the number of people and see the tip, the total and what each person pays, so that I can ask each person for the right amount straight away.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-1.1 to S-1.8.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-1.1 Given I open the page, when it has loaded, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2, and there is no error message and no result.
- S-1.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the tip amount is 15.00, the total is 115.00 and Each person pays lists 57.50 and 57.50.
- S-1.3 Given Tip % is 10 and People is 1, when I enter 60 in Bill, then the tip amount is 6.00, the total is 66.00 and Each person pays lists one amount, 66.00.
- S-1.4 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 1, when I enter 0.01 in Bill (the smallest bill), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01 and Each person pays lists one amount, 0.01.
- S-1.5 Given Tip % is 100 and People is 50, when I enter 1000000.00 in Bill (the largest bill), then the tip amount is 1000000.00, the total is 2000000.00 and Each person pays lists 40000.00 fifty times.
- S-1.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter Bill as ".5", "5.", "007" or "42.50" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.08, 0.75, 1.05 and 6.38 respectively.
- S-1.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 1, when I enter Tip % as ".5", "5." or "0015.00", then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.50, 5.00 and 15.00 respectively.
- S-1.8 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when I enter People as "04" or "4" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times.

## S-2 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Set the tip

As a Table Payer, I want to set the tip as a percentage and see what it comes to in money, so that I can agree on a tip that feels fair without guessing.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-2.1 to S-2.6.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-2.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I change Tip % from 15 to 20, then the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.
- S-2.2 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I enter 0 in Tip % (no tip), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 100.00 and Each person pays lists 50.00 and 50.00.
- S-2.3 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I enter 12.5 in Tip %, then the tip amount is 12.50, the total is 112.50 and Each person pays lists 56.25 and 56.25.
- S-2.4 Given Bill is 200 and People is 2, when I enter 7.25 in Tip % (two decimals), then the tip amount is 14.50, the total is 214.50 and Each person pays lists 107.25 and 107.25.
- S-2.5 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 0.30 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.05 (0.045 rounded half-up) and the total is 0.35.
- S-2.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 10.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 1.50, and when I change Bill to 10.05, then the tip amount is 1.51.

## S-3 (serves J-3, Not implemented): Share out the odd cents

As a Table Payer, I want to be told how the extra cents are shared out when the total does not divide evenly, so that what I collect adds up exactly to what I paid.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-3.1 to S-3.6.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-3.1 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the total is 100.00, Each person pays lists 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.2 Given Tip % is 18 and People is 3, when I enter 42.50 in Bill, then the tip amount is 7.65, the total is 50.15, Each person pays lists 16.72, 16.72 and 16.71, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 2 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.3 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 90 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 30.00 three times and no note about extra cents is shown.
- S-3.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 3, when I enter 0.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01, Each person pays lists 0.01, 0.00 and 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.5 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 50, when I enter 0.49 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 0.01 forty-nine times followed by 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.6 Given any valid Bill, Tip % and People, then the amounts in Each person pays add up exactly to the total, no two of them differ by more than 1 cent, and the larger amounts come first.

## S-4 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Get a clear message for an unusable entry

As a Table Payer, I want a clear message under any entry that cannot be used, so that I can correct the figure and never act on an amount built from a wrong one.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-4.1 to S-4.16.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-4.1 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "+5", "1e3", "4 2", ".", "1.2.3" or "٣", then "Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill has more than two decimals, such as "10.005", then "The bill can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Bill and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than a range message, for "0.005" and "1000000.001", which are also out of range.
- S-4.3 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "0", "0.00" or "0.", then "The bill must be at least 0.01." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "1000000.01" or a number with 400 digits, then "The bill cannot be more than 1000000.00." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.5 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is empty or only spaces, then "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.6 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "1e1", "." or "٣", then "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % has more than two decimals, such as "12.505", then "The tip can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Tip % and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than "The tip cannot be more than 100%.", for "100.001", which is also above the maximum.
- S-4.8 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is "100.01", "101" or a number with 400 digits, then "The tip cannot be more than 100%." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.9 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is empty or only spaces, then "Enter the number of people." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.10 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is not a whole number written with digits only, such as "2.5", "2.0", "2.", "abc", "-1", "1e1" or "٣", then "Enter the number of people as a whole number, like 4." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.11 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "0" or "00", then "There must be at least 1 person." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.12 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "51" or a number with 400 digits, then "There can be at most 50 people." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.13 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is empty or only spaces, then there is no error message and no result.
- S-4.14 Given Bill is "abc", Tip % is empty and People is "0", then each entry shows its own message under it ("Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50.", "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." and "There must be at least 1 person.") and there is no result.
- S-4.15 Given an entry cannot be used, when its message appears, then the message is directly under that entry and no other entry, inside a box marked aria-live="polite" that the entry is linked to with aria-describedby.
- S-4.16 Given any text in Bill, Tip % and People, including very long text, then nothing the page shows contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation.

## S-5 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Amounts follow every change

As a Table Payer, I want the amounts to follow every change I make, so that I never read out a figure that no longer matches what I entered.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-5.1 to S-5.7.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-5.1 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change People to 4, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times in place of 57.50 twice.
- S-5.2 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change Tip % to "abc", then the result disappears, "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip %, and no amount from before is left on the page.
- S-5.3 Given Bill is 100, People is 2 and Tip % is "abc" with its message showing, when I change Tip % to 18, then the message disappears and the result is shown: the tip amount is 18.00, the total is 118.00 and Each person pays lists 59.00 and 59.00.
- S-5.4 Given a result is showing, when I delete the Bill, then the result disappears and there is no error message.
- S-5.5 Given a result is showing, when I clear Tip %, then the result disappears and "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip %.
- S-5.6 Given Tip % is 15, People is 1 and Bill is empty, when I type 1, then 2, then 5 into Bill, then after each character the tip amount and total are 0.15 and 1.15, then 1.80 and 13.80, then 18.75 and 143.75, without my pressing anything.
- S-5.7 Given any Bill, Tip % and People, then the page never shows a result and an error message at the same time.

## S-6 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Start again

As a Table Payer, I want to clear everything and start again, so that nothing from the last bill carries over into the next one.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-6.1 to S-6.4.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-6.1 Given I have entered a Bill, changed Tip % to 20 and People to 4, and a result is showing, when I choose Reset, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2 and no result is shown.
- S-6.2 Given a message is showing under each of Bill, Tip % and People, when I choose Reset, then every message disappears.
- S-6.3 Given any state of the page, when I choose Reset, then the cursor is in the Bill entry, ready for typing.
- S-6.4 Given any entries, then the state after Reset is the same as the state when the page first opens: Bill empty, Tip % 15, People 2, no error message and no result.

## S-7 (serves J-5, Not implemented): Round the total up

As a Table Payer, I want to round the total up to a whole amount, so that I can pay in cash with the notes and coins I have, without waiting for change.

Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-7.1 to S-7.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-7.1 Given Bill is 41.20, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 47.38), when I choose to round the total up, then the total is 48.00 and Each person pays lists 24.00 and 24.00.
- S-7.2 Given Bill is 100, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 115.00), when I choose to round the total up, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays still lists 57.50 and 57.50.

## S-8 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Pick a quick tip

As a Table Payer, I want to choose a common tip with a single press, so that I can compare tips quickly while the table decides.

Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-8.1 to S-8.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-8.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I press the 20 button, then Tip % shows 20, the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.
- S-8.2 Given I pressed the 10 button, when I type 12.5 in Tip %, then the amounts follow 12.5 and no button is shown as chosen.

## Jobs not served in v1

- J-5 (Pay in cash without waiting for change) is served only by S-7, which is Not implemented.

## Out of scope for now

- Adding tax separately. The tip is worked out on the bill as entered. A separate tax entry would change what the tip is based on and needs its own entry, limits and messages.
- Splitting by items. The table has agreed to split equally. Splitting by what each person ordered is a different situation.

    "There must be at least 1 person.",

    "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more.",
]
for m in MESSAGES:
    if m not in doc:
        problems.append("message missing from doc: " + m)
quoted = set(re.findall(r'"([^"]{15,})"', doc))
for q in sorted(quoted):
    if q not in MESSAGES:
        problems.append("quoted text is not a known message: " + q)

for pat in (r"reviewer", r"assess", r"take-home", r"\bbrief\b", r"TODO", r"TBD", r"FIXME", r"\bno message\b", r"[\[\]<>]"):
    for m in re.finditer(pat, doc, re.I):

nonimpl = sum(1 for h in heads if h[2] == "Not implemented")

    served.setdefault(jid, []).append(sid)
for jid in job_ids:
    if jid not in served:
        problems.append(f"{jid} has no story")
print("jobs -> stories:", served)

# criteria per story
total = 0
no_when = []
sections = re.split(r"^## ", doc, flags=re.M)
for sec in sections:
    m = re.match(r"(S-\d+) \(serves", sec)
    if not m:
        continue
    sid = m.group(1)
    ids = re.findall(r"^- (" + sid + r"\.\d+) (.*)$", sec, re.M)
    nums = [int(i.split(".")[1]) for i, _ in ids]
    if nums != list(range(1, len(nums) + 1)):
        problems.append(f"{sid} criteria not sequential: {nums}")
    total += len(ids)
    note = re.search(r"^Status note: .*?(S-\d+\.\d+) to (S-\d+\.\d+)\.$", sec, re.M)
    if not note or note.group(1) != f"{sid}.1" or note.group(2) != f"{sid}.{len(nums)}":
        problems.append(f"{sid} status note does not match its {len(nums)} criteria")
    for cid, text in ids:
        if not text.startswith("Given "):
            problems.append(f"{cid} does not start with Given")
        if " when " not in text:
            no_when.append(cid)
        if " then " not in text:
            problems.append(f"{cid} has no then")
print("criteria total:", total)
print("criteria without 'when':", no_when)

    "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip.",
    "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5.",
    "The tip can have at most 2 decimal places.",
    "The tip cannot be more than 100%.",
    "Enter the number of people.",
    "Enter the number of people as a whole number, like 4.",
    "There must be at least 1 person.",
    "There can be at most 50 people.",
    "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more.",
    "The total does not divide evenly. The first 2 people pay 1 cent more.",
    "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more.",
]
for m in MESSAGES:
    if m not in doc:
        problems.append("message missing from doc: " + m)
quoted = set(re.findall(r'"([^"]{15,})"', doc))
for q in sorted(quoted):
    if q not in MESSAGES:
        problems.append("quoted text is not a known message: " + q)

for pat in (r"reviewer", r"assess", r"take-home", r"\bbrief\b", r"TODO", r"TBD", r"FIXME", r"\bno message\b", r"[\[\]<>]"):
    for m in re.finditer(pat, doc, re.I):
        line = doc.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
        problems.append(f"unwanted text {pat!r} on line {line}")

nonimpl = sum(1 for h in heads if h[2] == "Not implemented")
print("stories Not implemented:", nonimpl, "of", len(heads))
print("problems:", len(problems))
for p in problems:
    print(" -", p)
PYEOF

```markdown
# User Stories

Every story serves one job from the jobs document. A story is Implemented only when every one of its criteria has passed. Otherwise it is Not implemented, and a note names the criteria that have no evidence yet.

How to read the criteria:
- Bill, Tip % and People are the three entries. The page opens with Bill empty, Tip % showing 15 and People showing 2.
- Bill and Tip % take at least one digit and at most one decimal point. People takes digits only. Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces around an entry are ignored.
- The result has the tip amount (labelled Tip), the total (labelled Total, the bill plus the tip) and Each person pays, a numbered list with one amount per person. When the total does not divide evenly, a note about the extra cents appears in the result.
- Amounts have two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.
- Messages are quoted exactly as the page shows them. In a criterion about one entry, the other two entries are valid, so only that entry shows a message.

## S-1 (serves J-1, Not implemented): See what everyone owes

As a Table Payer, I want to enter the bill, the tip and the number of people and see the tip, the total and what each person pays, so that I can ask each person for the right amount straight away.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-1.1 to S-1.8.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-1.1 Given I open the page, when it has loaded, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2, and there is no error message and no result.
- S-1.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the tip amount is 15.00, the total is 115.00 and Each person pays lists 57.50 and 57.50.
- S-1.3 Given Tip % is 10 and People is 1, when I enter 60 in Bill, then the tip amount is 6.00, the total is 66.00 and Each person pays lists one amount, 66.00.
- S-1.4 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 1, when I enter 0.01 in Bill (the smallest bill), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01 and Each person pays lists one amount, 0.01.
- S-1.5 Given Tip % is 100 and People is 50, when I enter 1000000.00 in Bill (the largest bill), then the tip amount is 1000000.00, the total is 2000000.00 and Each person pays lists 40000.00 fifty times.
- S-1.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter Bill as ".5", "5.", "007" or "42.50" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.08, 0.75, 1.05 and 6.38 respectively.
- S-1.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 1, when I enter Tip % as ".5", "5." or "0015.00", then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.50, 5.00 and 15.00 respectively.
- S-1.8 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when I enter People as "04" or "4" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times.

## S-2 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Set the tip

As a Table Payer, I want to set the tip as a percentage and see what it comes to in money, so that I can agree on a tip that feels fair without guessing.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-2.1 to S-2.6.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-2.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I change Tip % from 15 to 20, then the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.
- S-2.2 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I enter 0 in Tip % (no tip), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 100.00 and Each person pays lists 50.00 and 50.00.
- S-2.3 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I enter 12.5 in Tip %, then the tip amount is 12.50, the total is 112.50 and Each person pays lists 56.25 and 56.25.
- S-2.4 Given Bill is 200 and People is 2, when I enter 7.25 in Tip % (two decimals), then the tip amount is 14.50, the total is 214.50 and Each person pays lists 107.25 and 107.25.
- S-2.5 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 0.30 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.05 (0.045 rounded half-up) and the total is 0.35.
- S-2.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 10.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 1.50, and when I change Bill to 10.05, then the tip amount is 1.51.

## S-3 (serves J-3, Not implemented): Share out the odd cents

As a Table Payer, I want to be told how the extra cents are shared out when the total does not divide evenly, so that what I collect adds up exactly to what I paid.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-3.1 to S-3.6.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-3.1 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the total is 100.00, Each person pays lists 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.2 Given Tip % is 18 and People is 3, when I enter 42.50 in Bill, then the tip amount is 7.65, the total is 50.15, Each person pays lists 16.72, 16.72 and 16.71, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 2 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.3 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 90 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 30.00 three times and no note about extra cents is shown.
- S-3.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 3, when I enter 0.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01, Each person pays lists 0.01, 0.00 and 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.5 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 50, when I enter 0.49 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 0.01 forty-nine times followed by 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
- S-3.6 Given any valid Bill, Tip % and People, when I enter them, then the amounts in Each person pays add up exactly to the total, no two of them differ by more than 1 cent, and the larger amounts come first.

## S-4 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Get a clear message for an unusable entry

As a Table Payer, I want a clear message under any entry that cannot be used, so that I can correct the figure and never act on an amount built from a wrong one.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-4.1 to S-4.16.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-4.1 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "+5", "1e3", "4 2", ".", "1.2.3" or "٣", then "Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill has more than two decimals, such as "10.005", then "The bill can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Bill and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than a range message, for "0.005" and "1000000.001", which are also out of range.
- S-4.3 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "0", "0.00" or "0.", then "The bill must be at least 0.01." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "1000000.01" or a number with 400 digits, then "The bill cannot be more than 1000000.00." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.5 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is empty or only spaces, then "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.6 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "1e1", "." or "٣", then "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % has more than two decimals, such as "12.505", then "The tip can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Tip % and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than "The tip cannot be more than 100%.", for "100.001", which is also above the maximum.
- S-4.8 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is "100.01", "101" or a number with 400 digits, then "The tip cannot be more than 100%." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.9 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is empty or only spaces, then "Enter the number of people." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.10 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is not a whole number written with digits only, such as "2.5", "2.0", "2.", "abc", "-1", "1e1" or "٣", then "Enter the number of people as a whole number, like 4." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.11 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "0" or "00", then "There must be at least 1 person." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.12 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "51" or a number with 400 digits, then "There can be at most 50 people." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.13 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is empty or only spaces, then there is no error message and no result.
- S-4.14 Given Tip % is empty and People is "0", when I enter "abc" in Bill, then each entry shows its own message under it ("Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50.", "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." and "There must be at least 1 person.") and there is no result.
- S-4.15 Given an entry cannot be used, when its message appears, then the message is directly under that entry and no other entry, inside a box marked aria-live="polite" that the entry is linked to with aria-describedby.
- S-4.16 Given any text in Bill, Tip % and People, including very long text, when I enter it, then nothing the page shows contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation.

## S-5 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Amounts follow every change

As a Table Payer, I want the amounts to follow every change I make, so that I never read out a figure that no longer matches what I entered.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-5.1 to S-5.7.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-5.1 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change People to 4, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times in place of 57.50 twice.
- S-5.2 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change Tip % to "abc", then the result disappears, "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip %, and no amount from before is left on the page.
- S-5.3 Given Bill is 100, People is 2 and Tip % is "abc" with its message showing, when I change Tip % to 18, then the message disappears and the result is shown: the tip amount is 18.00, the total is 118.00 and Each person pays lists 59.00 and 59.00.
- S-5.4 Given a result is showing, when I delete the Bill, then the result disappears and there is no error message.
- S-5.5 Given a result is showing, when I clear Tip %, then the result disappears and "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip %.
- S-5.6 Given Tip % is 15, People is 1 and Bill is empty, when I type 1, then 2, then 5 into Bill, then after each character the tip amount and total are 0.15 and 1.15, then 1.80 and 13.80, then 18.75 and 143.75, without my pressing anything.
- S-5.7 Given any Bill, Tip % and People, when I enter them, then the page never shows a result and an error message at the same time.

## S-6 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Start again

As a Table Payer, I want to clear everything and start again, so that nothing from the last bill carries over into the next one.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-6.1 to S-6.4.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-6.1 Given I have entered a Bill, changed Tip % to 20 and People to 4, and a result is showing, when I choose Reset, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2 and no result is shown.
- S-6.2 Given a message is showing under each of Bill, Tip % and People, when I choose Reset, then every message disappears.
- S-6.3 Given any state of the page, when I choose Reset, then the cursor is in the Bill entry, ready for typing.
- S-6.4 Given any entries, when I choose Reset, then the state is the same as when the page first opens: Bill empty, Tip % 15, People 2, no error message and no result.

## S-7 (serves J-5, Not implemented): Round the total up

As a Table Payer, I want to round the total up to a whole amount, so that I can pay in cash with the notes and coins I have, without waiting for change.

Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-7.1 to S-7.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-7.1 Given Bill is 41.20, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 47.38), when I choose to round the total up, then the total is 48.00 and Each person pays lists 24.00 and 24.00.
- S-7.2 Given Bill is 100, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 115.00), when I choose to round the total up, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays still lists 57.50 and 57.50.

## S-8 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Pick a quick tip

As a Table Payer, I want to choose a common tip with a single press, so that I can compare tips quickly while the table decides.

Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-8.1 to S-8.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-8.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I press the 20 button, then Tip % shows 20, the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.
- S-8.2 Given I pressed the 10 button, when I type 12.5 in Tip %, then the amounts follow 12.5 and no button is shown as chosen.

## Jobs not served in v1

- J-5 (Pay in cash without waiting for change) is served only by S-7, which is Not implemented.

## Out of scope for now

- Adding tax separately. The tip is worked out on the bill as entered. A separate tax entry would change what the tip is based on and needs its own entry, limits and messages.
- Splitting by items. The table has agreed to split equally. Splitting by what each person ordered is a different situation.
```

Checks run:
- **Arithmetic and entry rules.** A throwaway Python script outside the project checked every number in the examples. It also checked which message each example entry gets, plus 20,000 random trials of "shares add up, differ by at most 1 cent, larger first". It ran 60,182 checks with 0 failures. This tests my reading of your rules, not the app, which does not exist yet.
- **Structure.** All 8 stories point at an existing job, and every job has a story. The 51 criteria are numbered without gaps, each written as Given, when, then. Each status note covers its story's full range. All 15 quoted message strings are consistent, and none is misquoted. No reviewer or placeholder wording appears.
- **A slip I fixed.** My first structure check showed 5 criteria with no real "when" (S-3.6, S-4.14, S-4.16, S-5.7, S-6.4). I added one to each.

For you to check:
- **Not implemented stories.** I chose S-7, round the total up, which serves J-5, and S-8, quick-tip buttons, which serves J-2. Tax and splitting by items are listed as out of scope, each with a one-line reason.
- **Message wording.** The 12 error messages and the two note forms are my wording. They will go into the constants file exactly as quoted, so change any you dislike now.
- **S-4 and its job.** I tied S-4 to J-4 through "I find I used a wrong figure". It could also sit under J-1.
- **Statuses.** All eight say Not implemented because nothing is built. Each v1 story flips when all its criteria have evidence.
- **Size.** 51 criteria is about twice my earlier guess. The tests and the report scale with it.
- **Manual list candidates.** These depend on the page itself: S-1.1, S-4.15, S-5.1 to S-5.6 and S-6.1 to S-6.3.

import re
root = "/Users/laptop/mprojects/ahmad-sheraz-calculator/docs/"
roles = open(root + "app-roles.md", encoding="utf-8").read()

problems = []

# S-3.7 arithmetic, worked out with integers
bill, bp, n = 10000, 1800, 3
tip = (bill * bp + 5000) // 10000
total = bill + tip
base, r = divmod(total, n)
f = lambda c: f"{c // 100}.{c % 100:02d}"
shares = [f(base + 1)] * r + [f(base)] * (n - r)
if (f(tip), f(total), shares, r) != ("18.00", "118.00", ["39.34", "39.33", "39.33"], 1):
    problems.append(f"S-3.7 arithmetic differs: {f(tip)} {f(total)} {shares} {r}")

role_names = re.findall(r"^## (.+)$", roles, re.M)
job_ids = re.findall(r"^## (J-\d+) \((.+?)\): ", jobs, re.M)
job_role = dict(job_ids)
heads = re.findall(r"^## (S-\d+) \(serves (J-\d+), (Implemented|Not implemented)\): ", doc, re.M)

# traceability table against the headings, the jobs file and the roles file

    problems.append("table is not the end of the file")

per = {}
for sec in re.split(r"^## ", doc, flags=re.M):
    m = re.match(r"(S-\d+) \(serves", sec)
    if not m:
        continue
    sid = m.group(1)
    ids = re.findall(r"^- (" + sid + r"\.\d+) (.*)$", sec, re.M)
    nums = [int(i.split(".")[1]) for i, _ in ids]
    if nums != list(range(1, len(nums) + 1)):
        problems.append(f"{sid} criteria not sequential: {nums}")
    per[sid] = len(ids); total_ac += len(ids)
    note = re.search(r"^Status note: .*(S-\d+\.\d+) to (S-\d+\.\d+)\.$", sec, re.M)
    if not note or note.group(1) != f"{sid}.1" or note.group(2) != f"{sid}.{len(nums)}":
        problems.append(f"{sid} status note does not match its {len(nums)} criteria")
    for cid, text in ids:
        if not re.match(r"Given .+?, when .+?, then .+", text):
            problems.append(f"{cid} is not Given, when, then")

    "Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50.",
    "The bill can have at most 2 decimal places.",
    "The bill must be at least 0.01.",
    "The bill cannot be more than 1000000.00.",
    "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip.",
    "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5.",
    "The tip can have at most 2 decimal places.",
    "The tip cannot be more than 100%.",
    "Enter the number of people.",
    "Enter the number of people as a whole number, like 4.",
    "There must be at least 1 person.",
    "There can be at most 50 people.",
    "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more.",
    "The total does not divide evenly. The first 2 people pay 1 cent more.",
    "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more.",
}
for line in doc.splitlines():
    for q in re.findall(r'"([^"\n]+)"', line):
        if len(q) >= 15 and q not in MESSAGES:
            problems.append("quoted text is not a known message: " + q)
for pat in (r"reviewer", r"assess", r"take-home", r"\bbrief\b", r"TODO", r"TBD", r"FIXME", r"\bno message\b", r"[\[\]<>]"):
    for m in re.finditer(pat, doc, re.I):
        problems.append(f"unwanted text {pat!r} on line {doc.count(chr(10), 0, m.start()) + 1}")
print("criteria per story:", per, "| total:", total_ac)
print("table rows:", len(rows))
print("problems:", len(problems))
for p in problems:
    print(" -", p)
PYEOF

10	- Messages are quoted exactly as the page shows them. In a criterion about one entry, the other two entries are valid, so only that entry shows a message.
11	
12	## S-1 (serves J-1, Not implemented): See what everyone owes
13	
14	As a Table Payer, I want to enter the bill, the tip and the number of people and see the tip, the total and what each person pays, so that I can ask each person for the right amount straight away.
15	
16	Status note: no evidence yet for S-1.1 to S-1.8.
17

19	- S-1.1 Given I open the page, when it has loaded, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2, and there is no error message and no result.

21	- S-1.3 Given Tip % is 10 and People is 1, when I enter 60 in Bill, then the tip amount is 6.00, the total is 66.00 and Each person pays lists one amount, 66.00.
22	- S-1.4 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 1, when I enter 0.01 in Bill (the smallest bill), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01 and Each person pays lists one amount, 0.01.
23	- S-1.5 Given Tip % is 100 and People is 50, when I enter 1000000.00 in Bill (the largest bill), then the tip amount is 1000000.00, the total is 2000000.00 and Each person pays lists 40000.00 fifty times.
24	- S-1.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter Bill as ".5", "5.", "007" or "42.50" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.08, 0.75, 1.05 and 6.38 respectively.
25	- S-1.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 1, when I enter Tip % as ".5", "5." or "0015.00", then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.50, 5.00 and 15.00 respectively.
26	- S-1.8 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when I enter People as "04" or "4" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times.
27	
28	## S-2 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Set the tip
29	
30	As a Table Payer, I want to set the tip as a percentage and see what it comes to in money, so that I can agree on a tip that feels fair without guessing.
31	
32	Status note: no evidence yet for S-2.1 to S-2.6.
33

40	- S-2.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 10.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 1.50, and when I change Bill to 10.05, then the tip amount is 1.51.
41

43	
44	As a Table Payer, I want to be told how the extra cents are shared out when the total does not divide evenly, so that what I collect adds up exactly to what I paid.
45	
46	Status note: no evidence yet for S-3.1 to S-3.7.
47	
48	Acceptance criteria:
49	- S-3.1 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the total is 100.00, Each person pays lists 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.

51	- S-3.3 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 90 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 30.00 three times and no note about extra cents is shown.
52	- S-3.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 3, when I enter 0.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01, Each person pays lists 0.01, 0.00 and 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
53	- S-3.5 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 50, when I enter 0.49 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 0.01 forty-nine times followed by 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
54	- S-3.6 Given any valid Bill, Tip % and People, when I enter them, then the amounts in Each person pays add up exactly to the total, no two of them differ by more than 1 cent, and the larger amounts come first.
55	- S-3.7 Given Tip % is 18 and People is 3, when I enter 100.00 in Bill, then the tip amount is 18.00, the total is 118.00, Each person pays lists 39.34, 39.33 and 39.33, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
56	
57	## S-4 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Get a clear message for an unusable entry
58	
59	As a Table Payer, I want a clear message under any entry that cannot be used, so that I can correct the figure and never act on an amount built from a wrong one.
60	
61	Status note: no evidence yet for S-4.1 to S-4.16.
62	
63	Acceptance criteria:
64	- S-4.1 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "+5", "1e3", "4 2", ".", "1.2.3" or "٣", then "Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50." appears under Bill and there is no result.
65	- S-4.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill has more than two decimals, such as "10.005", then "The bill can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Bill and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than a range message, for "0.005" and "1000000.001", which are also out of range.
66	- S-4.3 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "0", "0.00" or "0.", then "The bill must be at least 0.01." appears under Bill and there is no result.
67	- S-4.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "1000000.01" or a number with 400 digits, then "The bill cannot be more than 1000000.00." appears under Bill and there is no result.
68	- S-4.5 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is empty or only spaces, then "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
69	- S-4.6 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "1e1", "." or "٣", then "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
70	- S-4.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % has more than two decimals, such as "12.505", then "The tip can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Tip % and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than "The tip cannot be more than 100%.", for "100.001", which is also above the maximum.
71	- S-4.8 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is "100.01", "101" or a number with 400 digits, then "The tip cannot be more than 100%." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
72	- S-4.9 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is empty or only spaces, then "Enter the number of people." appears under People and there is no result.
73	- S-4.10 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is not a whole number written with digits only, such as "2.5", "2.0", "2.", "abc", "-1", "1e1" or "٣", then "Enter the number of people as a whole number, like 4." appears under People and there is no result.
74	- S-4.11 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "0" or "00", then "There must be at least 1 person." appears under People and there is no result.
75	- S-4.12 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "51" or a number with 400 digits, then "There can be at most 50 people." appears under People and there is no result.
76	- S-4.13 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is empty or only spaces, then there is no error message and no result.
77	- S-4.14 Given Tip % is empty and People is "0", when I enter "abc" in Bill, then each entry shows its own message under it ("Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50.", "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." and "There must be at least 1 person.") and there is no result.
78	- S-4.15 Given an entry cannot be used, when its message appears, then the message is directly under that entry and no other entry, inside a box marked aria-live="polite" that the entry is linked to with aria-describedby.
79	- S-4.16 Given any text in Bill, Tip % and People, including very long text, when I enter it, then nothing the page shows contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation.
80	
81	## S-5 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Amounts follow every change
82	
83	As a Table Payer, I want the amounts to follow every change I make, so that I never read out a figure that no longer matches what I entered.
84	
85	Status note: no evidence yet for S-5.1 to S-5.7.
86	
87	Acceptance criteria:
88	- S-5.1 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change People to 4, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times in place of 57.50 twice.
89	- S-5.2 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change Tip % to "abc", then the result disappears, "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip %, and no amount from before is left on the page.
90	- S-5.3 Given Bill is 100, People is 2 and Tip % is "abc" with its message showing, when I change Tip % to 18, then the message disappears and the result is shown: the tip amount is 18.00, the total is 118.00 and Each person pays lists 59.00 and 59.00.
91	- S-5.4 Given a result is showing, when I delete the Bill, then the result disappears and there is no error message.
92	- S-5.5 Given a result is showing, when I clear Tip %, then the result disappears and "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip %.
93	- S-5.6 Given Tip % is 15, People is 1 and Bill is empty, when I type 1, then 2, then 5 into Bill, then after each character the tip amount and total are 0.15 and 1.15, then 1.80 and 13.80, then 18.75 and 143.75, without my pressing anything.
94	- S-5.7 Given any Bill, Tip % and People, when I enter them, then the page never shows a result and an error message at the same time.
95	
96	## S-6 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Start again
97	
98	As a Table Payer, I want to clear everything and start again, so that nothing from the last bill carries over into the next one.
99	
100	Status note: no evidence yet for S-6.1 to S-6.4.
101	
102	Acceptance criteria:
103	- S-6.1 Given I have entered a Bill, changed Tip % to 20 and People to 4, and a result is showing, when I choose Reset, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2 and no result is shown.
104	- S-6.2 Given a message is showing under each of Bill, Tip % and People, when I choose Reset, then every message disappears.
105	- S-6.3 Given any state of the page, when I choose Reset, then the cursor is in the Bill entry, ready for typing.
106	- S-6.4 Given any entries, when I choose Reset, then the state is the same as when the page first opens: Bill empty, Tip % 15, People 2, no error message and no result.
107	
108	## S-7 (serves J-5, Not implemented): Round the total up
109	
110	As a Table Payer, I want to round the total up to a whole amount, so that I can pay in cash with the notes and coins I have, without waiting for change.
111	
112	Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-7.1 to S-7.2.
113	
114	Acceptance criteria:
115	- S-7.1 Given Bill is 41.20, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 47.38), when I choose to round the total up, then the total is 48.00 and Each person pays lists 24.00 and 24.00.
116	- S-7.2 Given Bill is 100, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 115.00), when I choose to round the total up, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays still lists 57.50 and 57.50.
117	
118	## S-8 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Pick a quick tip
119	
120	As a Table Payer, I want to choose a common tip with a single press, so that I can compare tips quickly while the table decides.
121	
122	Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-8.1 to S-8.2.
123	
124	Acceptance criteria:
125	- S-8.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I press the 20 button, then Tip % shows 20, the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.
126	- S-8.2 Given I pressed the 10 button, when I type 12.5 in Tip %, then the amounts follow 12.5 and no button is shown as chosen.
127	
128	## Jobs not served in v1
129	
130	- J-5 (Pay in cash without waiting for change) is served only by S-7, which is Not implemented.
131	
132	## Out of scope for now
133	
134	- Adding tax separately. The tip is worked out on the bill as entered. A separate tax entry would change what the tip is based on and needs its own entry, limits and messages.
135	- Splitting by items. The table has agreed to split equally. Splitting by what each person ordered is a different situation.
136	
137	## Traceability
138	
139	| Story | Job | Role |
140	| --- | --- | --- |
141	| S-1 | J-1 | Table Payer |
142	| S-2 | J-2 | Table Payer |

- S-4.3 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "0", "0.00" or "0.", then "The bill must be at least 0.01." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "1000000.01" or a number with 400 digits, then "The bill cannot be more than 1000000.00." appears under Bill and there is no result.
- S-4.5 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is empty or only spaces, then "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.6 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "1e1", "." or "٣", then "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % has more than two decimals, such as "12.505", then "The tip can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Tip % and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than "The tip cannot be more than 100%.", for "100.001", which is also above the maximum.
- S-4.8 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when Tip % is "100.01", "101" or a number with 400 digits, then "The tip cannot be more than 100%." appears under Tip % and there is no result.
- S-4.9 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is empty or only spaces, then "Enter the number of people." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.10 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is not a whole number written with digits only, such as "2.5", "2.0", "2.", "abc", "-1", "1e1" or "٣", then "Enter the number of people as a whole number, like 4." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.11 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "0" or "00", then "There must be at least 1 person." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.12 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when People is "51" or a number with 400 digits, then "There can be at most 50 people." appears under People and there is no result.
- S-4.13 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is empty or only spaces, then there is no error message and no result.
- S-4.14 Given Tip % is empty and People is "0", when I enter "abc" in Bill, then each entry shows its own message under it ("Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50.", "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." and "There must be at least 1 person.") and there is no result.
- S-4.15 Given an entry cannot be used, when its message appears, then the message is directly under that entry and no other entry, inside a box marked aria-live="polite" that the entry is linked to with aria-describedby.
- S-4.16 Given any text in Bill, Tip % and People, including very long text, when I enter it, then nothing the page shows contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation.

## S-5 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Amounts follow every change

As a Table Payer, I want the amounts to follow every change I make, so that I never read out a figure that no longer matches what I entered.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-5.1 to S-5.7.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-5.1 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change People to 4, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times in place of 57.50 twice.
- S-5.2 Given a result is showing for Bill 100, Tip % 15 and People 2, when I change Tip % to "abc", then the result disappears, "Enter the tip using only digits and a decimal point, like 15 or 12.5." appears under Tip %, and no amount from before is left on the page.
- S-5.3 Given Bill is 100, People is 2 and Tip % is "abc" with its message showing, when I change Tip % to 18, then the message disappears and the result is shown: the tip amount is 18.00, the total is 118.00 and Each person pays lists 59.00 and 59.00.
- S-5.4 Given a result is showing, when I delete the Bill, then the result disappears and there is no error message.
- S-5.5 Given a result is showing, when I clear Tip %, then the result disappears and "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." appears under Tip %.
- S-5.6 Given Tip % is 15, People is 1 and Bill is empty, when I type 1, then 2, then 5 into Bill, then after each character the tip amount and total are 0.15 and 1.15, then 1.80 and 13.80, then 18.75 and 143.75, without my pressing anything.
- S-5.7 Given any Bill, Tip % and People, when I enter them, then the page never shows a result and an error message at the same time.

## S-6 (serves J-4, Not implemented): Start again

As a Table Payer, I want to clear everything and start again, so that nothing from the last bill carries over into the next one.

Status note: no evidence yet for S-6.1 to S-6.4.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-6.1 Given I have entered a Bill, changed Tip % to 20 and People to 4, and a result is showing, when I choose Reset, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2 and no result is shown.
- S-6.2 Given a message is showing under each of Bill, Tip % and People, when I choose Reset, then every message disappears.
- S-6.3 Given any state of the page, when I choose Reset, then the cursor is in the Bill entry, ready for typing.
- S-6.4 Given any entries, when I choose Reset, then the state is the same as when the page first opens: Bill empty, Tip % 15, People 2, no error message and no result.

## S-7 (serves J-5, Not implemented): Round the total up

As a Table Payer, I want to round the total up to a whole amount, so that I can pay in cash with the notes and coins I have, without waiting for change.

Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-7.1 to S-7.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-7.1 Given Bill is 41.20, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 47.38), when I choose to round the total up, then the total is 48.00 and Each person pays lists 24.00 and 24.00.
- S-7.2 Given Bill is 100, Tip % is 15 and People is 2 (the total is 115.00), when I choose to round the total up, then the total stays 115.00 and Each person pays still lists 57.50 and 57.50.

## S-8 (serves J-2, Not implemented): Pick a quick tip

As a Table Payer, I want to choose a common tip with a single press, so that I can compare tips quickly while the table decides.

Status note: left for a later version; no evidence for S-8.1 to S-8.2.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-8.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I press the 20 button, then Tip % shows 20, the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.

- J-5 (Pay in cash without waiting for change) is served only by S-7, which is Not implemented.

## Out of scope for now

- Adding tax separately. The tip is worked out on the bill as entered. A separate tax entry would change what the tip is based on and needs its own entry, limits and messages.
- Splitting by items. The table has agreed to split equally. Splitting by what each person ordered is a different situation.

| Story | Job | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S-1 | J-1 | Table Payer |
| S-2 | J-2 | Table Payer |
| S-3 | J-3 | Table Payer |
| S-4 | J-4 | Table Payer |
| S-5 | J-4 | Table Payer |
| S-6 | J-4 | Table Payer |
| S-7 | J-5 | Table Payer |
| S-8 | J-2 | Table Payer |

1	# Project rules
2	
3	This is a take-home assignment for a Product Engineering role: a tip and bill splitter that runs in a web browser. I direct the work, review everything and test the app myself. You write the code and help me draft three product documents, in this order: docs/app-roles.md, docs/jobs-to-be-done.md and docs/user-stories.md.
4	
5	## What good looks like
6	- A small app that fully works and is well specified beats a big one that doesn't.
7	- The documents and the README must describe exactly what was built. Never claim something works unless it was verified.
8	- Every claim in a doc or the README is backed by a passing test, a command that was run, or a check that was done and recorded. If something was not checked, say so plainly.
9	- A story is Implemented only when every one of its acceptance criteria has passed, by an automated test or by a manual check I confirmed. Otherwise it is Not implemented.
10	
11	## Technical rules
12	- Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No build step, no dependencies, no frameworks and no ES modules, so the app opens by double-clicking src/index.html.
13	- Nothing is loaded from outside: no network requests, no external fonts or libraries.
14	- Logic lives in plain CommonJS-style files that also load as classic browser scripts and through require() in Node. package.json must not set "type": "module".
15	- Money is integer cents. Never use floating point for amounts.
16	- Keep the UI thin. app.js only reads the fields, calls the pure view-model function and writes the result to the page. No money logic and no message text in app.js.
17	- Every message the user can see lives in one constants file, and the docs quote those exact strings.
18	- Never show NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation on the page.
19	- Tests use node:test and run with `node --test` on Node 20 or newer. Test files are named *.test.js, and test names start with the criterion id, such as S-1.1. Tests that guard the docs or the page files start with DOCS- or PAGE- instead of a criterion id. Keep the tests free of anything newer than Node 20.
20	
21	## Working rules
22	- Don't add features, dependencies or files beyond what we agree. Ask before large changes.
23	- If a criterion in the docs looks wrong or impossible, tell me. Don't change it quietly.
24	- Don't say something is verified in a browser unless you ran it there. I check browser behavior myself.
25	- If I edit anything by hand, I'll tell you, and it goes in the README.
26	- Commit locally after each stage (setup, docs, logic and tests, UI, fixes, test report and README) with a clear message. Never push and never add a remote.
27	- Keep the assessment and the reviewers out of code comments, UI text and the three product docs. The README can mention that this is a take-home.
28	- Don't copy the assignment brief into any file in this repository, except the unedited transcript.
29	- Keep replies short and in plain English, and say what you changed.
30	- Run `npm test` before you call a stage done, and report the real counts.
31	- To show that the tests catch bugs, plant one bug at a time in a throwaway copy outside the project, never in the working tree, and say which test failed.
32	- Leave no placeholders (TODO or bracketed fill-ins) in a committed file. If you need a fact only I have, such as a model name or a browser version, ask me.
33	- Keep temporary tooling out of the project. If a preview server needs a config file, it goes in the git-ignored .claude/ folder and is deleted afterwards.
34	
35	## Decisions
36	
37	### Product
38	- One role: a person at a restaurant table who pays the check and tells everyone what they owe. The split is equal. Don't invent a second role.
39	- The one real "must never" is showing a wrong or stale amount: shares that don't add up to the total, or an old result after an input became invalid. Don't invent others.
40	- The inputs are the bill amount, the tip percentage (default 15) and the number of people (default 2).
41	- Live as I type, the app shows the tip, the total, each person's share and a line saying how an uneven split is shared. It has a Reset button.
42	- Not in v1: quick-tip buttons, rounding the total up, splitting by items, adding tax separately. Two of them, which we choose when we write the stories, are documented as Not implemented stories. The others are listed as out of scope.
43	- I test by hand in Chrome and Safari. The README and the test report list only the browsers I actually tested, with their versions.
44	- I publish the repo on GitHub (public) and push it myself at the end.
45	
46	### Money
47	- Integer cents only, as above. The tip percentage is stored as basis points (15% is 1500).
48	- The tip is the bill as entered times the percentage, rounded half-up to the cent, once, on the whole bill. The total is the bill plus the tip.
49	- If the total doesn't divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first people. The result says so. The shares add up exactly to the total.
50	- Limits: bill 0.01 to 1000000.00, tip 0 to 100 with up to two decimals, people 1 to 50 as whole numbers. Anything else gets a clear message and no result.
51	- A bill of 0.01 split three ways (0.01, 0.00, 0.00) is allowed and shown honestly.
52	
53	### Inputs and display
54	- All three fields are text fields that we validate ourselves. Bill and tip use inputmode="decimal". People uses inputmode="numeric". No input type=number: it returns an empty value for invalid text, so we can't tell empty from invalid.
55	- Bill and tip: digits plus one optional decimal point, at most two decimals. ".5" and "5." are fine. "." on its own is not.
56	- People: digits only. "2.5", "2.0" and "2." are rejected.
57	- All three: leading zeros are fine ("007" is 7). Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces at the ends are ignored. Commas, signs, exponents, letters and digits from other scripts are rejected.
58	- If a value has too many decimals and is also out of range (a bill of 0.005), the decimals message wins.
59	- An empty bill is never an error: there is just no result yet. That covers the first open, the state after Reset, and a bill I delete. An empty tip field or an empty people field is an error with its own message.
60	- Amounts show two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators, so what you read is what you can type.
61	
62	### UI
63	- One pure function takes the raw input strings and returns everything the page shows: messages, formatted amounts, which fields are in error, the split line and the state after Reset. app.js only reads the fields, calls it and writes the result to the page. That way I can test the messages without a browser.
64	- Static labels (field names, button text, headings) are not messages and stay in index.html. The every-message rule covers only text the app produces at run time, such as errors, results and the split line.
65	- Each message shows under the field that caused it, in an aria-live="polite" box linked to the input.
66	- The Result box is emptied and hidden whenever any entry is invalid, so a message and an old amount never show together.
67	- The shares are a numbered list under "Each person pays".
68	- The button is called Reset. It puts the defaults back, clears every message and moves focus to the Bill field.
69	- The page works at 320 px wide and with the keyboard alone.
70	
71	### Tests
72	- The tests should be a real strength, not a small suite.
73	- Unit tests for each acceptance criterion.
74	- Invariant tests with a seeded random generator. They print the seed when one fails, and the SEED environment variable replays it, as in `SEED=12345 npm test`.
75	- A test for every on-screen message.
76	- A test that fails if the docs and the code drift apart.
77	- Page-file tests read index.html, styles.css and app.js as text. They check the script order, that nothing is loaded from outside, that app.js holds no message text or money logic, and that every id, label and live box is in place.
78	- All of it runs with a plain `npm test` (which runs `node --test`). Nothing to install.
79	
80	### Docs and status
81	- Statuses follow the evidence. A criterion changes only if the criterion itself was wrong, and you tell me first. Never weaken a criterion to make it pass.
82	- Criteria that depend on the page itself (live updating, messages appearing and disappearing, Reset, the first open) sit in a manual list in the docs-sync test. They need a browser check that I confirmed.
83	- A page-dependent criterion counts as passed only when I confirmed it in every browser the README lists. The README lists only browsers I actually tested.
84	- A story that isn't Implemented gets a one-line status note naming the criteria that have no evidence.
85	- Check each criterion's own numbers against the default of 2 people. The leftover note shows for every total with an odd number of cents, so write "no error message", not "no message", unless the total divides evenly.
86	- docs/test-report.md has: how to run the tests; the last run with real counts; the browsers tested (name, version, operating system, date, checks, who ran them); one row per criterion (how it was verified, and pass, fail, not confirmed or not built); and a list of what is not covered. Only what is true goes in.
87	
88	### README
89	- It describes only what exists and works.
90	- No badges and no screenshots.
91	- It says which commands were actually run, and on which system.
92	- Ask me for the model name. Don't guess it.

I read both files and wrote no code and no files. I also noted your point on README item 4. The sentence about reloading goes in only if you test reload in each browser. I put reload on the browser checklist in section 4.

### 1. Files
```
src/messages.js    every run-time string: 12 error messages, 2 note forms
src/calc.js        validate, tip, split, format. No DOM, no text of its own
src/viewmodel.js   viewModel(), resetState()
src/app.js         DOM glue
src/index.html     labels, headings, message boxes, Reset (static text)
src/styles.css
tests/stories.test.js     one test per automated criterion
tests/edge-cases.test.js  odd inputs
tests/invariants.test.js  seeded random (small generator inside, no helper file)
tests/messages.test.js    one test per message
tests/docs.test.js        DOCS- tests
tests/page.test.js        PAGE- tests
```
Each src file is wrapped so it loads with `require()` in Node and as a classic script that attaches to one global, `TipSplit`. No ES modules. Script order: messages, calc, viewmodel, app.

### 2. Functions
```js
// calc.js
validateBill(text)   // { ok: true, value: cents } | { ok: false, code, message }
validateTip(text)    // { ok: true, value: basisPoints } | { ok: false, code, message }
validatePeople(text) // { ok: true, value: count } | { ok: false, code, message }
tipCents(billCents, basisPoints) // integer cents, half-up, rounded once
splitTotal(totalCents, people)   // { shares: [cents, ...], extra }   extra = total % people
formatCents(cents)               // "12.34"
LIMITS                           // the numbers behind the limits
```
- **Validators never throw and never return NaN.** They trim spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces. They check an ASCII-digit grammar and decide the range by digit count. Only then do they make a number.
- **Error codes.** `code` is `empty`, `invalid`, `decimals`, `min` or `max`. `message` is looked up in messages.js.
- **Empty entries.** An empty bill returns `{ ok: false, code: 'empty', message: null }`, which is not an error. An empty tip or empty people returns its own message. Non-string input counts as empty.
- **Arithmetic functions.** `tipCents`, `splitTotal` and `formatCents` take already-validated integers. Anything else returns `null`.

```js
// viewmodel.js
viewModel({ bill, tip, people })   // the three raw strings
// {
//   fields: { bill: { invalid, message }, tip: {...}, people: {...} },   // message "" when fine
//   result: null | { tip: "15.00", total: "115.00", shares: ["57.50", "57.50"], note: "" }
// }
resetState()  // { values: { bill: "", tip: "15", people: "2" }, view: viewModel(values) }
```
- `result` is `null` when any field is invalid or the bill is empty.
- `note` is `""` unless the total does not divide evenly. Then it holds one of the two note messages.
- It is pure: the same strings give the same output, with no touched flag, and it never throws.
- The state after Reset is the defaults run through `viewModel`, so there are no messages and no result.

### 3. app.js
- **Reads** the three `.value` strings.
- **Calls** `viewModel` on every `input` event, and `resetState` on load and on Reset.
- **Writes** each field's message text and `aria-invalid`. It writes the Result box too: `hidden`, tip, total, one `<li>` per share, and the note. After Reset it calls `focus()` on Bill.
- **Never does** parsing, arithmetic or text of its own.

**Live, not a button.** It is your decision. A button would also let an old result stay on screen after an entry changed, which is the one thing the app must never do. The `input` event, unlike `keyup`, also catches paste.

**Page rules:**
- No `<form>`, so Enter cannot reload the page.
- No `maxlength`, so the 400-digit criteria can be entered.
- Inputs get `autocomplete="off"`, and app.js writes the opening values on load. That way browser form-restore cannot leave stale fields after a reload.

### 4. Tests
All use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` only, so nothing is newer than Node 20.

| Criteria | Covered by |
|---|---|
| S-1.2 to S-1.5, S-2.1 to S-2.6, S-3.1 to S-3.5, S-3.7 | stories test, with the docs' exact numbers typed by hand |
| S-1.6 to S-1.8 | stories test plus edge cases (spaces, tab, NBSP, leading zeros) |
| S-3.6 | invariants I1, I2 |
| S-4.1 to S-4.12 | stories test (every example entry) plus edge cases plus message tests |
| S-4.13, S-4.14 | stories test |
| S-4.16 | invariant I6, after the rewording below |
| S-5.7 | invariant I5 |
| S-6.4 | stories test plus I7 |
| S-1.1, S-4.15, S-5.1 to S-5.6, S-6.1 to S-6.3 (11) | manual in Chrome and Safari |
| S-7.1, S-7.2, S-8.1, S-8.2 | none (Not implemented) |

The manual criteria also get automated support where possible. That means `resetState` values for S-1.1, S-6.1 and S-6.2, view-model output for S-5.1 to S-5.6, and PAGE- markup tests for S-4.15. It does not replace your check.

**Edge cases** (names start with the nearest criterion id plus "edge"):
- An em space at the ends must fail. Inner spaces fail too.
- `10.000`, `0.`, `.`, `..`, `5.5.5`.
- 400 digits and 400 zeros.
- Full-width and Arabic digits, a U+2212 minus, `1e3`, `0x10`, the words `NaN` and `Infinity`, and non-string input.
- The bound `100000000 * 10000 + 5000 < 2^53`.

**Invariants** (seeded, 2,000 cases each, a new seed per run). The seed is printed in the failure message, and `SEED=12345 npm test` replays it.
- **I1:** shares add up to the total.
- **I2:** shares differ by at most 1 cent, never increase, and exactly `total % people` of them are larger.
- **I3:** the tip is the half-up rounding. In integers, `10000*tip <= bill*rate + 5000 < 10000*(tip+1)`.
- **I4:** total equals bill plus tip, and every amount is whole cents within bounds.
- **I5:** a result and a message never appear together. An empty bill gives neither.
- **I6:** no NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent in any output, for hostile text up to 400 characters.
- **I7:** the same input gives the same output, the input is not mutated, and `resetState()` equals `viewModel(defaults)` after any other calls.
- **I8:** the validators never throw and always return a boolean `ok`.

**Message tests:** a 14-row table of key, criterion, trigger entries and exact text from the docs. A last test fails if messages.js holds a message that is not in the table.

**DOCS- tests:**
1. messages.js and the quotes in user-stories.md match, both ways. The `{count}` form is checked with the docs' examples.
2. Every criterion has a test, is on the manual list, or sits in a Not implemented story. No test id is missing from the docs.
3. Status matches evidence. Implemented needs every criterion tested, or manual and confirmed in test-report.md. Not implemented needs a note naming the unproven ones.
4. The traceability table matches the story headings, and the jobs and role exist.
5. The limits written in the messages equal `LIMITS`.

**PAGE- tests:**
- Script order.
- Nothing external: URLs, `@import`, fetch, XHR, `import()`.
- app.js has no message strings and none of `parseFloat|parseInt|Number(|toFixed|Math.|BigInt`.
- Labels, ids, `inputmode`, `autocomplete`, `aria-describedby` pointing at an `aria-live="polite"` box, Result `hidden`, `<ol>` under "Each person pays", and the Reset button.
- No `<form>`, no `maxlength`, and CSS keeps `[hidden]` hidden.

These are text checks, so they are heuristics. Their limits go in the report's "not covered".

**Your browser checklist (Chrome and Safari):** the 11 manual criteria, plus 320 px width, keyboard only, and reload. None of the last three is a criterion, so the report records them as checks.

### 5. The five riskiest places
1. **Float math and `toFixed`.** `(0.3*0.15).toFixed(2)` gives `0.04` in Node (checked), and half-up gives 0.05. Guard:
   - integer cents and basis points only;
   - no text goes through `Number()` or `parseFloat`;
   - trap values in S-2.5 and S-2.6;
   - I3.
2. **Rounding in the wrong place or twice**, such as per-person tips or a rounded total. Guard: one rounding, on the whole-bill tip, with an exact total. I3 and I4 check it.
3. **Lost or doubled cents in the split.** Guard: only `total % people` extra cents, to the first people. I1 and I2 check it, with S-3.4 (total smaller than the headcount) and S-3.5 (49 of 50).
4. **Bad text becoming a number.** Examples are empty becoming 0, `1e3`, `٣`, 400 digits becoming Infinity or an exponent, and people 0 dividing by zero. Guard:
   - the grammar check comes first;
   - the range is decided by digit count;
   - a number is made only after both;
   - edge cases, I6 and I8.
5. **A stale amount after an entry changes or becomes unusable.** Guard: a pure view-model, a page that rewrites everything on each `input` and empties the Result box, I5, and the manual S-5 checks.

### 6. Build order
1. `messages.js`, plus the messages-to-docs test.
2. `calc.js` validators, with the S-4 and edge-case tests.
3. `calc.js` tip, split and format, with the S-1 to S-3 tests and I1 to I4 and I8.
4. `viewmodel.js`, with the S-5 and S-6.4 tests, the message tests, and I5 to I7.
5. `docs.test.js`. Then `npm test`, report the real counts, and stop for your review. No commit yet.
6. After your approval: commit "logic and tests". Then the UI (`index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`, PAGE- tests), your browser checks, fixes, planted-bug demos, `docs/test-report.md`, statuses and the README. `npm test` runs after every step.

**One criterion needs your call.** S-4.16 cannot hold as written. It says nothing the page shows contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation. If someone types `NaN` or `1e3` into Bill, the entry itself shows it. The intent is text the app produces. My proposed wording is: "...then no message, amount or note that the page produces contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation." I have not changed it.

Steps 1 to 5 are built and not committed.

**`npm test` on Node v24.21.0:** tests 101, pass 101, fail 0, exit code 0.

| File | Tests |
|---|---|
| `tests/stories.test.js` | 43 |
| `tests/edge-cases.test.js` | 27 |
| `tests/messages.test.js` | 14 |
| `tests/invariants.test.js` | 8 |
| `tests/docs.test.js` | 9 |

**Your three changes:**
1. **S-4.16 reworded.** It now ends "...then no message, amount or note that the page produces contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation." `git diff` shows that one line changed in [docs/user-stories.md](docs/user-stories.md).
2. **Fixed seed.** The default seed is 1. Two `npm test` runs gave identical results apart from timings. `SEED=12345 npm test` also passed 101 of 101. `SEED=abc` fails with "SEED must be a whole number from 0 to 4294967295".
   - **Failure prints the seed.** I checked this in a throwaway copy in the scratchpad, outside the project. I planted one bug in `splitTotal` (`i < extra` became `i <= extra`). With `SEED=777`, the two S-3.6 invariant tests failed, "shares add up exactly to the total" and "shares differ by at most 1 cent...". Each message starts "failed with SEED=777 at case 0" and ends with the replay hint. The default run printed `SEED=1`.
3. **Separate lists in [tests/docs.test.js](tests/docs.test.js).**
   - **Labelled lists.** `MANUAL` holds the 11 page-dependent criteria. `NOT_BUILT` holds S-7.1, S-7.2, S-8.1 and S-8.2. DOCS-5 checks that the not-built ones have no tests, and nothing there reads story status.
   - **Two-way message check.** DOCS-1 and DOCS-2 count a quoted string as a message only if it starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, so "abc", "5." and ".5" are skipped.

**Files:** [src/messages.js](src/messages.js), [src/calc.js](src/calc.js), [src/viewmodel.js](src/viewmodel.js) and the five test files above.

**Where I differed from the plan:**
- **Combined steps.** I wrote steps 2 and 3 together, because `calc.js` is one file. All eight invariants went into step 4, because they run through `viewModel`, which did not exist at step 3.
- **Status check deferred.** DOCS-9 checks only that each status is valid and that a status note names the story's own criteria. All eight stories are Not implemented now, so a check that statuses match evidence cannot hold yet. I will add it with `docs/test-report.md`.
- **A mistake I caught.** My first DOCS-3 check also counted regex `.test(` calls as test calls, so DOCS-3, DOCS-4 and DOCS-5 failed (98 of 101 passed). I fixed it by counting only top-level `test('...')` calls.

**Checked, not run on Node 20:**
- `grep` found no newer APIs, for example `toSorted`, `structuredClone` or `Object.groupBy`.
- The only `parseFloat` or `Number` match in `src` is a comment in `calc.js`. No code converts text with them.
- There is no TODO or reviewer wording in `src` or `tests`.

**For you to check in the code:**
- Non-string entries such as `undefined` or a number count as empty text, so `viewModel` never throws.
- `splitTotal` also returns `null` for fewer than 1 or more than 50 people.
- The many-people note is a `{count}` template in `messages.js`, filled in by `viewmodel.js`.

The commit will include the S-4.16 rewording.

**1. The test where an error clears.** It is `S-5.3 (support) changing Tip % from abc to 18 removes the message and shows the result`, at [tests/stories.test.js:266](tests/stories.test.js:266).
- It runs `viewModel` for Bill 100, Tip % "abc", People 2. That gives only the Tip % message and no result.
- It then runs `viewModel` for Bill 100, Tip % 18, People 2. That gives no messages and tip 18.00, total 118.00, shares 59.00 and 59.00.
- `S-5.2 (support)` at line 261 checks the opposite direction.
- This test covers what `viewModel` returns. Whether the page actually clears the message is still the manual check for S-5.3, and the page is not built yet.

**2. Entries 999999.99, 1e5 and 12,50.**
- **999999.99:** it was covered only as a Bill entry. `S-4.4 edge: Bill limit boundaries` accepts it as 99999999 cents. `S-2.5 edge: tips on a tie...` uses it at a 100% tip.
- **1e5:** no test used it. The suite only had 1e3, 1E3, 1e+3, 1e-3 and 1e1.
- **12,50:** no test used it. The suite only had 1,5 and 1,000.

I added five edge tests at the end of [tests/edge-cases.test.js](tests/edge-cases.test.js). No existing test changed.
- `S-4.1 edge: Bill of 1e5 or 12,50 is unusable`
- `S-4.6 edge: Tip % of 1e5 or 12,50 is unusable`
- `S-4.10 edge: People of 1e5 or 12,50 is unusable`
- `S-4.4 edge: 999999.99 is usable as Bill, above the maximum as Tip % and not a whole number as People`
- `S-1.5 edge: a bill of 999999.99 at 15% for 2 people works end to end`

The first three check the validator code and the exact message shown by `viewModel`, with no result. The last one expects tip 150000.00, total 1149999.99, shares 575000.00 and 574999.99, and the one-person note. I worked those numbers out in a separate script before writing the test. The new tests are not committed.
