# Project rules

This is a take-home assignment for a Product Engineering role: a tip and bill splitter that runs in a web browser. I direct the work, review everything and test the app myself. You write the code and help me draft three product documents, in this order: docs/app-roles.md, docs/jobs-to-be-done.md and docs/user-stories.md.

## What good looks like
- A small app that fully works and is well specified beats a big one that doesn't.
- The documents and the README must describe exactly what was built. Never claim something works unless it was verified.
- Every claim in a doc or the README is backed by a passing test, a command that was run, or a check that was done and recorded. If something was not checked, say so plainly.
- A story is Implemented only when every one of its acceptance criteria has passed, by an automated test or by a manual check I confirmed. Otherwise it is Not implemented.

## Technical rules
- Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No build step, no dependencies, no frameworks and no ES modules, so the app opens by double-clicking src/index.html.
- Nothing is loaded from outside: no network requests, no external fonts or libraries.
- Logic lives in plain CommonJS-style files that also load as classic browser scripts and through require() in Node. package.json must not set "type": "module".
- Money is integer cents. Never use floating point for amounts.
- Keep the UI thin. app.js only reads the fields, calls the pure view-model function and writes the result to the page. No money logic and no message text in app.js.
- Every message the user can see lives in one constants file, and the docs quote those exact strings.
- Never show NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation on the page.
- Tests use node:test and run with `node --test` on Node 20 or newer. Test files are named *.test.js, and test names start with the criterion id, such as S-1.1. Tests that guard the docs or the page files start with DOCS- or PAGE- instead of a criterion id. Keep the tests free of anything newer than Node 20.

## Working rules
- Don't add features, dependencies or files beyond what we agree. Ask before large changes.
- If a criterion in the docs looks wrong or impossible, tell me. Don't change it quietly.
- Don't say something is verified in a browser unless you ran it there. I check browser behavior myself.
- If I edit anything by hand, I'll tell you, and it goes in the README.
- Commit locally after each stage (setup, docs, logic and tests, UI, fixes, test report and README) with a clear message. Never push and never add a remote.
- Keep the assessment and the reviewers out of code comments, UI text and the three product docs. The README can mention that this is a take-home.
- Don't copy the assignment brief into any file in this repository, except the unedited transcript.
- Keep replies short and in plain English, and say what you changed.
- Run `npm test` before you call a stage done, and report the real counts.
- To show that the tests catch bugs, plant one bug at a time in a throwaway copy outside the project, never in the working tree, and say which test failed.
- Leave no placeholders (TODO or bracketed fill-ins) in a committed file. If you need a fact only I have, such as a model name or a browser version, ask me.
- Keep temporary tooling out of the project. If a preview server needs a config file, it goes in the git-ignored .claude/ folder and is deleted afterwards.

## Decisions

### Product
- One role: a person at a restaurant table who pays the check and tells everyone what they owe. The split is equal. Don't invent a second role.
- The one real "must never" is showing a wrong or stale amount: shares that don't add up to the total, or an old result after an input became invalid. Don't invent others.
- The inputs are the bill amount, the tip percentage (default 15) and the number of people (default 2).
- Live as I type, the app shows the tip, the total, each person's share and a line saying how an uneven split is shared. It has a Reset button.
- Not in v1: quick-tip buttons, rounding the total up, splitting by items, adding tax separately. Two of them, which we choose when we write the stories, are documented as Not implemented stories. The others are listed as out of scope.
- I test by hand in Chrome and Safari. The README and the test report list only the browsers I actually tested, with their versions.
- I publish the repo on GitHub (public) and push it myself at the end.

### Money
- Integer cents only, as above. The tip percentage is stored as basis points (15% is 1500).
- The tip is the bill as entered times the percentage, rounded half-up to the cent, once, on the whole bill. The total is the bill plus the tip.
- If the total doesn't divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first people. The result says so. The shares add up exactly to the total.
- Limits: bill 0.01 to 1000000.00, tip 0 to 100 with up to two decimals, people 1 to 50 as whole numbers. Anything else gets a clear message and no result.
- A bill of 0.01 split three ways (0.01, 0.00, 0.00) is allowed and shown honestly.

### Inputs and display
- All three fields are text fields that we validate ourselves. Bill and tip use inputmode="decimal". People uses inputmode="numeric". No input type=number: it returns an empty value for invalid text, so we can't tell empty from invalid.
- Bill and tip: digits plus one optional decimal point, at most two decimals. ".5" and "5." are fine. "." on its own is not.
- People: digits only. "2.5", "2.0" and "2." are rejected.
- All three: leading zeros are fine ("007" is 7). Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces at the ends are ignored. Commas, signs, exponents, letters and digits from other scripts are rejected.
- If a value has too many decimals and is also out of range (a bill of 0.005), the decimals message wins.
- An empty bill is never an error: there is just no result yet. That covers the first open, the state after Reset, and a bill I delete. An empty tip field or an empty people field is an error with its own message.
- Amounts show two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators, so what you read is what you can type.

### UI
- One pure function takes the raw input strings and returns everything the page shows: messages, formatted amounts, which fields are in error, the split line and the state after Reset. app.js only reads the fields, calls it and writes the result to the page. That way I can test the messages without a browser.
- Static labels (field names, button text, headings) are not messages and stay in index.html. The every-message rule covers only text the app produces at run time, such as errors, results and the split line.
- Each message shows under the field that caused it, in an aria-live="polite" box linked to the input.
- The Result box is emptied and hidden whenever any entry is invalid, so a message and an old amount never show together.
- The shares are a numbered list under "Each person pays".
- The button is called Reset. It puts the defaults back, clears every message and moves focus to the Bill field.
- The page works at 320 px wide and with the keyboard alone.

### Tests
- The tests should be a real strength, not a small suite.
- Unit tests for each acceptance criterion.
- Invariant tests with a seeded random generator. They print the seed when one fails, and the SEED environment variable replays it, as in `SEED=12345 npm test`.
- A test for every on-screen message.
- A test that fails if the docs and the code drift apart.
- Page-file tests read index.html, styles.css and app.js as text. They check the script order, that nothing is loaded from outside, that app.js holds no message text or money logic, and that every id, label and live box is in place.
- All of it runs with a plain `npm test` (which runs `node --test`). Nothing to install.

### Docs and status
- Statuses follow the evidence. A criterion changes only if the criterion itself was wrong, and you tell me first. Never weaken a criterion to make it pass.
- Criteria that depend on the page itself (live updating, messages appearing and disappearing, Reset, the first open) sit in a manual list in the docs-sync test. They need a browser check that I confirmed.
- A page-dependent criterion counts as passed only when I confirmed it in every browser the README lists. The README lists only browsers I actually tested.
- A story that isn't Implemented gets a one-line status note naming the criteria that have no evidence.
- Check each criterion's own numbers against the default of 2 people. The leftover note shows for every total with an odd number of cents, so write "no error message", not "no message", unless the total divides evenly.
- docs/test-report.md has: how to run the tests; the last run with real counts; the browsers tested (name, version, operating system, date, checks, who ran them); one row per criterion (how it was verified, and pass, fail, not confirmed or not built); and a list of what is not covered. Only what is true goes in.

### README
- It describes only what exists and works.
- No badges and no screenshots.
- It says which commands were actually run, and on which system.
- Ask me for the model name. Don't guess it.

docs_test = read("tests", "docs.test.js")


def list_from(name):
    block = re.search(r"const " + name + r" = \[(.*?)\];", docs_test, re.S).group(1)
    return re.findall(r"'(S-\d+\.\d+)'", block)


MANUAL = list_from("MANUAL")
NOT_BUILT = list_from("NOT_BUILT")

names = []
for file in sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(root, "tests"))):
    if file.endswith(".test.js"):
        names += re.findall(r"^test\(\s*'([^'\n]*)'", read("tests", file), re.M)
assert all("|" not in name and "; " not in name for name in names), "a test name has a pipe or a semicolon"

ids = re.findall(r"^- (S-\d+\.\d+) ", read("docs", "user-stories.md"), re.M)


def primary(criterion):
    own = [name for name in names if name.startswith(criterion + " ")]
    plain = [name for name in own
             if " edge:" not in name and " message:" not in name and "(support)" not in name and " invariant:" not in name]
    return plain if plain else [name for name in own if " invariant:" in name]

1	# User Stories
2	
3	Every story serves one job from the jobs document. A story is Implemented only when every one of its criteria is covered by a passing automated test or by a manual check confirmed in a browser. Otherwise it is Not implemented, and a note names the criteria that have no evidence. The automated tests never load the page: they run the logic, and the page's script against a stand-in page. A criterion that depends on the page itself counts only with a manual check confirmed in Chrome and Safari. The results are in docs/test-report.md.
4	
5	How to read the criteria:
6	- Bill, Tip % and People are the three entries. The page opens with Bill empty, Tip % showing 15 and People showing 2.
7	- Bill and Tip % take at least one digit and at most one decimal point. People takes digits only. Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces around an entry are ignored.
8	- The result has the tip amount (labelled Tip), the total (labelled Total, the bill plus the tip) and Each person pays, a numbered list with one amount per person. When the total does not divide evenly, a note about the extra cents appears in the result.
9	- Amounts have two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.
10	- Messages are quoted exactly as the page shows them. In a criterion about one entry, the other two entries are valid, so only that entry shows a message.
11	
12	## S-1 (serves J-1, Implemented): See what everyone owes
13	
14	As a Table Payer, I want to enter the bill, the tip and the number of people and see the tip, the total and what each person pays, so that I can ask each person for the right amount straight away.
15	
16	Evidence: S-1.1 by a manual check in Chrome and Safari; S-1.2 to S-1.8 by automated tests only, which never load the page.
17	
18	Acceptance criteria:
19	- S-1.1 Given I open the page, when it has loaded, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2, and there is no error message and no result.
20	- S-1.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the tip amount is 15.00, the total is 115.00 and Each person pays lists 57.50 and 57.50.
21	- S-1.3 Given Tip % is 10 and People is 1, when I enter 60 in Bill, then the tip amount is 6.00, the total is 66.00 and Each person pays lists one amount, 66.00.
22	- S-1.4 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 1, when I enter 0.01 in Bill (the smallest bill), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01 and Each person pays lists one amount, 0.01.
23	- S-1.5 Given Tip % is 100 and People is 50, when I enter 1000000.00 in Bill (the largest bill), then the tip amount is 1000000.00, the total is 2000000.00 and Each person pays lists 40000.00 fifty times.
24	- S-1.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter Bill as ".5", "5.", "007" or "42.50" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.08, 0.75, 1.05 and 6.38 respectively.
25	- S-1.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 1, when I enter Tip % as ".5", "5." or "0015.00", then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.50, 5.00 and 15.00 respectively.
26	- S-1.8 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when I enter People as "04" or "4" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times.
27	
28	## S-2 (serves J-2, Implemented): Set the tip
29	
30	As a Table Payer, I want to set the tip as a percentage and see what it comes to in money, so that I can agree on a tip that feels fair without guessing.
31	
32	Evidence: S-2.1 to S-2.6 by automated tests only, which never load the page.

# User Stories

Every story serves one job from the jobs document. A story is Implemented only when every one of its criteria is covered by a passing automated test or by a manual check confirmed in a browser. Otherwise it is Not implemented, and a note names the criteria that have no evidence. The automated tests never load the page: they run the logic, and the page's script against a stand-in page. A criterion that depends on the page itself counts only with a manual check confirmed in Chrome and Safari. The results are in docs/test-report.md.

How to read the criteria:
- Bill, Tip % and People are the three entries. The page opens with Bill empty, Tip % showing 15 and People showing 2.
- Bill and Tip % take at least one digit and at most one decimal point. People takes digits only. Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces around an entry are ignored.
- The result has the tip amount (labelled Tip), the total (labelled Total, the bill plus the tip) and Each person pays, a numbered list with one amount per person. When the total does not divide evenly, a note about the extra cents appears in the result.
- Amounts have two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.
- Messages are quoted exactly as the page shows them. In a criterion about one entry, the other two entries are valid, so only that entry shows a message.

## S-1 (serves J-1, Implemented): See what everyone owes

As a Table Payer, I want to enter the bill, the tip and the number of people and see the tip, the total and what each person pays, so that I can ask each person for the right amount straight away.

Evidence: S-1.1 by a manual check in Chrome and Safari; S-1.2 to S-1.8 by automated tests only, which never load the page.

Acceptance criteria:
- S-1.1 Given I open the page, when it has loaded, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2, and there is no error message and no result.
- S-1.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the tip amount is 15.00, the total is 115.00 and Each person pays lists 57.50 and 57.50.
- S-1.3 Given Tip % is 10 and People is 1, when I enter 60 in Bill, then the tip amount is 6.00, the total is 66.00 and Each person pays lists one amount, 66.00.
- S-1.4 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 1, when I enter 0.01 in Bill (the smallest bill), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01 and Each person pays lists one amount, 0.01.
- S-1.5 Given Tip % is 100 and People is 50, when I enter 1000000.00 in Bill (the largest bill), then the tip amount is 1000000.00, the total is 2000000.00 and Each person pays lists 40000.00 fifty times.
- S-1.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter Bill as ".5", "5.", "007" or "42.50" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.08, 0.75, 1.05 and 6.38 respectively.
- S-1.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 1, when I enter Tip % as ".5", "5." or "0015.00", then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.50, 5.00 and 15.00 respectively.
- S-1.8 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when I enter People as "04" or "4" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times.

## S-2 (serves J-2, Implemented): Set the tip

As a Table Payer, I want to set the tip as a percentage and see what it comes to in money, so that I can agree on a tip that feels fair without guessing.

Evidence: S-2.1 to S-2.6 by automated tests only, which never load the page.

Acceptance criteria:

- S-2.4 Given Bill is 200 and People is 2, when I enter 7.25 in Tip % (two decimals), then the tip amount is 14.50, the total is 214.50 and Each person pays lists 107.25 and 107.25.
- S-2.5 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 0.30 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.05 (0.045 rounded half-up) and the total is 0.35.
- S-2.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 10.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 1.50, and when I change Bill to 10.05, then the tip amount is 1.51.

content.content:
1	# User Stories
2	
3	Every story serves one job from the jobs document. A story is Implemented only when every one of its criteria is covered by a passing automated test or by a manual check confirmed in a browser. Otherwise it is Not implemented, and a note names the criteria that have no evidence. The automated tests never load the page: they run the logic, and the page's script against a stand-in page. A criterion that depends on the page itself counts only with a manual check confirmed in Chrome and Safari. The results are in docs/test-report.md.
4	
5	How to read the criteria:
6	- Bill, Tip % and People are the three entries. The page opens with Bill empty, Tip % showing 15 and People showing 2.
7	- Bill and Tip % take at least one digit and at most one decimal point. People takes digits only. Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces around an entry are ignored.
8	- The result has the tip amount (labelled Tip), the total (labelled Total, the bill plus the tip) and Each person pays, a numbered list with one amount per person. When the total does not divide evenly, a note about the extra cents appears in the result.
9	- Amounts have two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.
10	- Messages are quoted exactly as the page shows them. In a criterion about one entry, the other two entries are valid, so only that entry shows a message.
11	
12	## S-1 (serves J-1, Implemented): See what everyone owes
13	
14	As a Table Payer, I want to enter the bill, the tip and the number of people and see the tip, the total and what each person pays, so that I can ask each person for the right amount straight away.
15	
16	Evidence: S-1.1 by a manual check in Chrome and Safari; S-1.2 to S-1.8 by automated tests only, which never load the page.
17	
18	Acceptance criteria:
19	- S-1.1 Given I open the page, when it has loaded, then Bill is empty, Tip % shows 15, People shows 2, and there is no error message and no result.
20	- S-1.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the tip amount is 15.00, the total is 115.00 and Each person pays lists 57.50 and 57.50.
21	- S-1.3 Given Tip % is 10 and People is 1, when I enter 60 in Bill, then the tip amount is 6.00, the total is 66.00 and Each person pays lists one amount, 66.00.
22	- S-1.4 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 1, when I enter 0.01 in Bill (the smallest bill), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01 and Each person pays lists one amount, 0.01.
23	- S-1.5 Given Tip % is 100 and People is 50, when I enter 1000000.00 in Bill (the largest bill), then the tip amount is 1000000.00, the total is 2000000.00 and Each person pays lists 40000.00 fifty times.
24	- S-1.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter Bill as ".5", "5.", "007" or "42.50" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.08, 0.75, 1.05 and 6.38 respectively.
25	- S-1.7 Given Bill is 100 and People is 1, when I enter Tip % as ".5", "5." or "0015.00", then there is no error message and the tip amount is 0.50, 5.00 and 15.00 respectively.
26	- S-1.8 Given Bill is 100 and Tip % is 15, when I enter People as "04" or "4" with spaces, tabs or non-breaking spaces around it, then there is no error message and Each person pays lists 28.75 four times.
27	
28	## S-2 (serves J-2, Implemented): Set the tip
29	
30	As a Table Payer, I want to set the tip as a percentage and see what it comes to in money, so that I can agree on a tip that feels fair without guessing.
31	
32	Evidence: S-2.1 to S-2.6 by automated tests only, which never load the page.
33	
34	Acceptance criteria:
35	- S-2.1 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I change Tip % from 15 to 20, then the tip amount is 20.00, the total is 120.00 and Each person pays lists 60.00 and 60.00.
36	- S-2.2 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I enter 0 in Tip % (no tip), then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 100.00 and Each person pays lists 50.00 and 50.00.
37	- S-2.3 Given Bill is 100 and People is 2, when I enter 12.5 in Tip %, then the tip amount is 12.50, the total is 112.50 and Each person pays lists 56.25 and 56.25.
38	- S-2.4 Given Bill is 200 and People is 2, when I enter 7.25 in Tip % (two decimals), then the tip amount is 14.50, the total is 214.50 and Each person pays lists 107.25 and 107.25.
39	- S-2.5 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 0.30 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.05 (0.045 rounded half-up) and the total is 0.35.
40	- S-2.6 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 1, when I enter 10.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 1.50, and when I change Bill to 10.05, then the tip amount is 1.51.
41	
42	## S-3 (serves J-3, Implemented): Share out the odd cents
43	
44	As a Table Payer, I want to be told how the extra cents are shared out when the total does not divide evenly, so that what I collect adds up exactly to what I paid.
45	
46	Evidence: S-3.1 to S-3.7 by automated tests only, which never load the page.
47	
48	Acceptance criteria:
49	- S-3.1 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 100 in Bill, then the total is 100.00, Each person pays lists 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
50	- S-3.2 Given Tip % is 18 and People is 3, when I enter 42.50 in Bill, then the tip amount is 7.65, the total is 50.15, Each person pays lists 16.72, 16.72 and 16.71, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 2 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
51	- S-3.3 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 3, when I enter 90 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 30.00 three times and no note about extra cents is shown.
52	- S-3.4 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 3, when I enter 0.01 in Bill, then the tip amount is 0.00, the total is 0.01, Each person pays lists 0.01, 0.00 and 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
53	- S-3.5 Given Tip % is 0 and People is 50, when I enter 0.49 in Bill, then Each person pays lists 0.01 forty-nine times followed by 0.00, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first 49 people pay 1 cent more." is shown.
54	- S-3.6 Given any valid Bill, Tip % and People, when I enter them, then the amounts in Each person pays add up exactly to the total, no two of them differ by more than 1 cent, and the larger amounts come first.
55	- S-3.7 Given Tip % is 18 and People is 3, when I enter 100.00 in Bill, then the tip amount is 18.00, the total is 118.00, Each person pays lists 39.34, 39.33 and 39.33, and the note "The total does not divide evenly. The first person pays 1 cent more." is shown.
56	
57	## S-4 (serves J-4, Implemented): Get a clear message for an unusable entry
58	
59	As a Table Payer, I want a clear message under any entry that cannot be used, so that I can correct the figure and never act on an amount built from a wrong one.
60	
61	Evidence: S-4.15 by a manual check in Chrome and Safari; S-4.1 to S-4.14 and S-4.16 by automated tests only, which never load the page.
62	
63	Acceptance criteria:
64	- S-4.1 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is not a number written with digits and at most one decimal point, such as "abc", "1,5", "-5", "+5", "1e3", "4 2", ".", "1.2.3" or "٣", then "Enter the bill using only digits and a decimal point, like 42.50." appears under Bill and there is no result.
65	- S-4.2 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill has more than two decimals, such as "10.005", then "The bill can have at most 2 decimal places." appears under Bill and there is no result; the same message appears, rather than a range message, for "0.005" and "1000000.001", which are also out of range.
66	- S-4.3 Given Tip % is 15 and People is 2, when Bill is "0", "0.00" or "0.", then "The bill must be at least 0.01." appears under Bill and there is no result.

They must never be shown a wrong or out-of-date amount: shares that do not add up exactly to the total, or an earlier result that is still showing after what they entered has changed or stopped being usable.

# Jobs To Be Done

## J-1 (Table Payer): Tell everyone what they owe

When the bill arrives and my table has agreed to split it equally, I want to know exactly what each person owes, tip included, so I can ask each of them for the right amount straight away and settle up.

## J-2 (Table Payer): Settle on a tip

When the table is deciding how much to tip, I want to find out what each tip we are considering would come to in actual money, so I can agree on one that feels fair without guessing.

## J-3 (Table Payer): Share out the odd cents

When the amount we have to pay cannot be divided into equal amounts of whole cents, I want to know exactly how the extra cents are shared out, so I can collect exactly what I paid, with no arguments about odd cents and no shortfall for me to cover.

## J-4 (Table Payer): Redo the sums when things change

When something changes (the table changes its mind, someone joins or leaves, or I find I used a wrong figure) or another bill needs splitting, I want to redo the sums from the corrected figures or from scratch, so I can be sure nothing I tell anyone is based on a wrong or out-of-date figure.

## J-5 (Table Payer): Pay in cash without waiting for change

When I am paying the bill in cash, I want to hand over an amount I can make up from the notes and coins I have on me, so I can pay straight away without waiting for change.

1	# App Roles
2	
3	## Table Payer
4	
5	A Table Payer is a person having a meal at a restaurant with friends, family or coworkers, anywhere from two people to a large table. The group has agreed to split the bill equally, and this person settles it with the restaurant, so they pay the whole amount and then have to collect each person's share. They want to add a fair tip and tell everyone exactly what they owe, quickly, while the table waits, without doing sums by hand or arguing over odd cents. What they collect has to add up to what they paid, bill and tip together, because any shortfall comes out of their own pocket. They can enter the bill, a tip percentage and the number of people; see the tip, the total (bill plus tip) and each person's share as they type; see how any leftover cents are shared when the total does not divide evenly; get a clear message when something they entered cannot be used; and start again for the next bill. They must never be shown a wrong or out-of-date amount: shares that do not add up exactly to the total, or an earlier result that is still showing after what they entered has changed or stopped being usable.
6

1	# Jobs To Be Done
2	
3	## J-1 (Table Payer): Tell everyone what they owe
4	
5	When the bill arrives and my table has agreed to split it equally, I want to know exactly what each person owes, tip included, so I can ask each of them for the right amount straight away and settle up.
6	
7	## J-2 (Table Payer): Settle on a tip
8	
9	When the table is deciding how much to tip, I want to find out what each tip we are considering would come to in actual money, so I can agree on one that feels fair without guessing.
10	
11	## J-3 (Table Payer): Share out the odd cents
12	
13	When the amount we have to pay cannot be divided into equal amounts of whole cents, I want to know exactly how the extra cents are shared out, so I can collect exactly what I paid, with no arguments about odd cents and no shortfall for me to cover.
14	
15	## J-4 (Table Payer): Redo the sums when things change
16	
17	When something changes (the table changes its mind, someone joins or leaves, or I find I used a wrong figure) or another bill needs splitting, I want to redo the sums from the corrected figures or from scratch, so I can be sure nothing I tell anyone is based on a wrong or out-of-date figure.
18	
19	## J-5 (Table Payer): Pay in cash without waiting for change
20	
21	When I am paying the bill in cash, I want to hand over an amount I can make up from the notes and coins I have on me, so I can pay straight away without waiting for change.
22

# Test report

## How to run the tests

From the project folder, with Node 20 or newer. Nothing to install.

```bash
npm test
```

`SEED=12345 npm test` runs the seeded random tests with a different seed. A seeded test that fails prints the seed it used.

## Last run

2026-10-23 on macOS 15.7.5, with Node v24.21.0 and npm 11.19.0: 125 tests ran, 125 passed, 0 failed.

## Browsers tested

I opened the page myself in each browser and typed the entries by hand, as a normal user would.

| Browser | Version | Operating system | Date | Checks | Run by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Chrome | 156.0.8078.48 | macOS 15.7.5 | 2026-10-23 | S-1.1, S-4.15, S-5.1 to S-5.6, S-6.1 to S-6.3 | me |
| Safari | 18.6 | macOS 15.7.5 | 2026-10-23 | S-1.1, S-4.15, S-5.1 to S-5.6, S-6.1 to S-6.3 | me |

All 11 checks passed in both browsers. None failed and none was left untested. These are the only browsers with results in this report.

"How verified" is the name of the main automated test for the criterion, or "manual, confirmed by me". Many criteria also have edge-case, message and invariant tests whose names start with the same id. An automated row shows pass because every test in the last run above passed.

# Project rules

This is a take-home assignment for a Product Engineering role: a tip and bill splitter that runs in a web browser. I direct the work, review everything and test the app myself. You write the code and help me draft three product documents, in this order: docs/app-roles.md, docs/jobs-to-be-done.md and docs/user-stories.md.

## What good looks like
- A small app that fully works and is well specified beats a big one that doesn't.
- The documents and the README must describe exactly what was built. Never claim something works unless it was verified.
- Every claim in a doc or the README is backed by a passing test, a command that was run, or a check that was done and recorded. If something was not checked, say so plainly.
- A story is Implemented only when every one of its acceptance criteria has passed, by an automated test or by a manual check I confirmed. Otherwise it is Not implemented.

## Technical rules
- Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No build step, no dependencies, no frameworks and no ES modules, so the app opens by double-clicking src/index.html.
- Nothing is loaded from outside: no network requests, no external fonts or libraries.
- Logic lives in plain CommonJS-style files that also load as classic browser scripts and through require() in Node. package.json must not set "type": "module".
- Money is integer cents. Never use floating point for amounts.
- Keep the UI thin. app.js only reads the fields, calls the pure view-model function and writes the result to the page. No money logic and no message text in app.js.
- Every message the user can see lives in one constants file, and the docs quote those exact strings.
- Never show NaN, Infinity, undefined or exponent notation on the page.
- Tests use node:test and run with `node --test` on Node 20 or newer. Test files are named *.test.js, and test names start with the criterion id, such as S-1.1. Tests that guard the docs or the page files start with DOCS- or PAGE- instead of a criterion id. Keep the tests free of anything newer than Node 20.

## Working rules
- Don't add features, dependencies or files beyond what we agree. Ask before large changes.
- If a criterion in the docs looks wrong or impossible, tell me. Don't change it quietly.
- Don't say something is verified in a browser unless you ran it there. I check browser behavior myself.
- If I edit anything by hand, I'll tell you, and it goes in the README.
- Commit locally after each stage (setup, docs, logic and tests, UI, fixes, test report and README) with a clear message. Never push and never add a remote.
- Keep the assessment and the reviewers out of code comments, UI text and the three product docs. The README can mention that this is a take-home.
- Don't copy the assignment brief into any file in this repository, except the unedited transcript.
- Keep replies short and in plain English, and say what you changed.
- Run `npm test` before you call a stage done, and report the real counts.
- To show that the tests catch bugs, plant one bug at a time in a throwaway copy outside the project, never in the working tree, and say which test failed.
- Leave no placeholders (TODO or bracketed fill-ins) in a committed file. If you need a fact only I have, such as a model name or a browser version, ask me.
- Keep temporary tooling out of the project. If a preview server needs a config file, it goes in the git-ignored .claude/ folder and is deleted afterwards.

## Decisions

### Product
- One role: a person at a restaurant table who pays the check and tells everyone what they owe. The split is equal. Don't invent a second role.
- The one real "must never" is showing a wrong or stale amount: shares that don't add up to the total, or an old result after an input became invalid. Don't invent others.
- The inputs are the bill amount, the tip percentage (default 15) and the number of people (default 2).
- Live as I type, the app shows the tip, the total, each person's share and a line saying how an uneven split is shared. It has a Reset button.
- Not in v1: quick-tip buttons, rounding the total up, splitting by items, adding tax separately. Two of them, which we choose when we write the stories, are documented as Not implemented stories. The others are listed as out of scope.
- I test by hand in Chrome and Safari. The README and the test report list only the browsers I actually tested, with their versions.
- I publish the repo on GitHub (public) and push it myself at the end.

### Money
- Integer cents only, as above. The tip percentage is stored as basis points (15% is 1500).
- The tip is the bill as entered times the percentage, rounded half-up to the cent, once, on the whole bill. The total is the bill plus the tip.
- If the total doesn't divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first people. The result says so. The shares add up exactly to the total.
- Limits: bill 0.01 to 1000000.00, tip 0 to 100 with up to two decimals, people 1 to 50 as whole numbers. Anything else gets a clear message and no result.
- A bill of 0.01 split three ways (0.01, 0.00, 0.00) is allowed and shown honestly.

### Inputs and display
- All three fields are text fields that we validate ourselves. Bill and tip use inputmode="decimal". People uses inputmode="numeric". No input type=number: it returns an empty value for invalid text, so we can't tell empty from invalid.
- Bill and tip: digits plus one optional decimal point, at most two decimals. ".5" and "5." are fine. "." on its own is not.
- People: digits only. "2.5", "2.0" and "2." are rejected.
- All three: leading zeros are fine ("007" is 7). Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces at the ends are ignored. Commas, signs, exponents, letters and digits from other scripts are rejected.
- If a value has too many decimals and is also out of range (a bill of 0.005), the decimals message wins.
- An empty bill is never an error: there is just no result yet. That covers the first open, the state after Reset, and a bill I delete. An empty tip field or an empty people field is an error with its own message.
- Amounts show two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators, so what you read is what you can type.

### UI
- One pure function takes the raw input strings and returns everything the page shows: messages, formatted amounts, which fields are in error, the split line and the state after Reset. app.js only reads the fields, calls it and writes the result to the page. That way I can test the messages without a browser.
- Static labels (field names, button text, headings) are not messages and stay in index.html. The every-message rule covers only text the app produces at run time, such as errors, results and the split line.
- Each message shows under the field that caused it, in an aria-live="polite" box linked to the input.
- The Result box is emptied and hidden whenever any entry is invalid, so a message and an old amount never show together.
- The shares are a numbered list under "Each person pays".
- The button is called Reset. It puts the defaults back, clears every message and moves focus to the Bill field.
- The page works at 320 px wide and with the keyboard alone.

### Tests
- The tests should be a real strength, not a small suite.
- Unit tests for each acceptance criterion.
- Invariant tests with a seeded random generator. They print the seed when one fails, and the SEED environment variable replays it, as in `SEED=12345 npm test`.
- A test for every on-screen message.
- A test that fails if the docs and the code drift apart.
- Page-file tests read index.html, styles.css and app.js as text. They check the script order, that nothing is loaded from outside, that app.js holds no message text or money logic, and that every id, label and live box is in place.
- All of it runs with a plain `npm test` (which runs `node --test`). Nothing to install.

### Docs and status
- Statuses follow the evidence. A criterion changes only if the criterion itself was wrong, and you tell me first. Never weaken a criterion to make it pass.
- Criteria that depend on the page itself (live updating, messages appearing and disappearing, Reset, the first open) sit in a manual list in the docs-sync test. They need a browser check that I confirmed.
- A page-dependent criterion counts as passed only when I confirmed it in every browser the README lists. The README lists only browsers I actually tested.
- A story that isn't Implemented gets a one-line status note naming the criteria that have no evidence.
- Check each criterion's own numbers against the default of 2 people. The leftover note shows for every total with an odd number of cents, so write "no error message", not "no message", unless the total divides evenly.
- docs/test-report.md has: how to run the tests; the last run with real counts; the browsers tested (name, version, operating system, date, checks, who ran them); one row per criterion (how it was verified, and pass, fail, not confirmed or not built); and a list of what is not covered. Only what is true goes in.

### README
- It describes only what exists and works.
- No badges and no screenshots.
- It says which commands were actually run, and on which system.
- Ask me for the model name. Don't guess it.

## Technical rules
- Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No build step, no dependencies, no frameworks and no ES modules, so the app opens by double-clicking src/index.html.

### Product
- One role: a person at a restaurant table who pays the check and tells everyone what they owe. The split is equal. Don't invent a second role.

- If the total doesn't divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first people. The result says so. The shares add up exactly to the total.

content.content:
I found no wrong amount, no stale result and no crash in the current code. What I found are confusing moments, a rounding trap for reviewers who cross-check, a layout edge case, and one large gap in the tests. I fixed nothing: `git status` is clean and HEAD is still `7e12085`. My scripts are in the scratchpad, outside the project.

## What I ran
- **Money:** 402,000 cases through the real code, checked against an independent Python `Fraction` oracle. 150,000 were random and 252,000 were exact half-cent ties. There were 0 mismatches in tip, total, shares or note.
- **Page, in the DOM:** 8,000 random edits and Resets (849 Resets), checking invariants after every step. There were 0 failures.
  - No result appeared with a message, and the hidden Result box was always empty.
  - `aria-invalid` matched the messages, and shares summed to the total.
  - The share count matched People, and the page matched `viewModel`.
  - After every Reset, focus was on Bill and no message remained.
- **Hostile sizes:** 5 MB entries in all three fields took 42 ms or less, with no crash.
- **Other checkouts:** a copy with Windows line endings and a copy in a folder path with spaces both passed 114 of 114.
- **Other seeds:** the invariant tests pass with 27 other seeds.
- **Where I ran the page:** the built-in browser pane, Chrome-based, served from a temporary localhost server that I stopped. The 8,000-step walk used synthetic `input` events, and the keystroke checks used real keystrokes. It was not `file://`, and not Safari.

## Findings, most likely to be met first
1. **Messages flash while someone is still typing.** This is by design but noisy. Steps, with real keystrokes in the pane:
   - Click Bill and type `0`. "The bill must be at least 0.01." shows, and it stays at `0.`. Type `5` and it clears.
   - Start with `.` and the "digits and a decimal point" message shows until a digit arrives.
   - Click Tip %, press End, then Backspace twice. "Enter a tip percentage. Use 0 for no tip." shows once the field is empty. Type `2` and it clears.
   - People should do the same by the view-model, but I only typed it for Tip %.
2. **A float calculator disagrees by one cent, and the app is the one that is right.** Steps:
   - Enter Bill 1.05, Tip % 10, People 1. The app shows Tip 0.11. `(1.05*10/100).toFixed(2)` in a JS console gives "0.10".
   - Enter Bill 10.10, Tip % 15. The app shows 1.52. Python `round(10.10*15/100, 2)` gives 1.51.
   - Across 99,505 grid cases (bills 1.00 to 200.00 at 10, 12.5, 15, 18 and 20%), a float calculator disagrees in 2,823, only on exact half-cents.
   - Nothing on screen says "rounded half-up", so the README has to.
3. **Nothing on the page explains the entries.** On opening there is no hint whether People includes the payer, whether Bill includes tax, or how the tip is rounded. Large amounts also show without separators, for example `2000000.00`, by decision.

# Tip and Bill Splitter

A web page that splits a restaurant bill equally, adds a tip and shows what each person owes. It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript: no build step, no dependencies and no network use. This is a take-home assignment for a Product Engineering role.

## What it is, who it is for, and why

You enter the bill, a tip percentage (15 to start) and the number of people (2 to start). As you type, the page shows the tip, the total and what each person pays. When the total cannot be split into equal cents, it says how the extra cents are shared. Reset starts again.

It is for one role, the Table Payer: a person at a restaurant table who settles the whole bill and then has to collect each person's share. The group has agreed to split equally, and any shortfall comes out of the payer's own pocket ([docs/app-roles.md](docs/app-roles.md)).

```
package.json       the test script and the Node version; no dependencies
.gitignore
docs/
  app-roles.md
  jobs-to-be-done.md
  user-stories.md
  test-report.md
src/               the app

  styles.css

transcripts/       the transcripts of the Claude Code sessions
```

# Tip and Bill Splitter

A web page that splits a restaurant bill equally, adds a tip and shows what each person owes. It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript: no build step, no dependencies and no network use. This is a take-home assignment for a Product Engineering role.

## What it is, who it is for, and why

You enter the bill, a tip percentage (15 to start) and the number of people (2 to start). As you type, the page shows the tip, the total and what each person pays. When the total cannot be split into equal cents, it says how the extra cents are shared. Reset starts again.

It is for one role, the Table Payer: a person at a restaurant table who settles the whole bill and then has to collect each person's share. The group has agreed to split equally, and any shortfall comes out of the payer's own pocket ([docs/app-roles.md](docs/app-roles.md)).

I chose it because the person, the jobs and the one thing that must never happen are small and clear enough to write down and test. I wanted a small app that fully works and is well specified, not a big one that does not. The jobs ([docs/jobs-to-be-done.md](docs/jobs-to-be-done.md)) are:

- J-1 Tell everyone what they owe.
- J-2 Settle on a tip.
- J-3 Share out the odd cents.
- J-4 Redo the sums when things change.
- J-5 Pay in cash without waiting for change. Not served in this version.

The one thing that must never happen is showing a wrong or out-of-date amount: shares that do not add up exactly to the total, or an old result still on screen after an entry became unusable.

## Prerequisites

- A current web browser, to run the app. Only Chrome and Safari were tested (see [Browsers tested](#browsers-tested)).
- Node.js 20 or newer, only to run the tests. The tests were run on Node v24.21.0 (npm 11.19.0). They were not run on Node 20.

## Commands

No install step. The project has no dependencies, so there is no `npm install`.

Open the app:

- macOS: double-click `src/index.html`, or run `open src/index.html`.
- Windows: double-click `src\index.html`, or run `start src\index.html` in Command Prompt or PowerShell.
- Linux: double-click `src/index.html` in the file manager, or run `xdg-open src/index.html`.

Run the tests:

```bash
npm test
```

The invariant tests use random cases from a seed. Without a seed they use seed 1, so every run gives the same result. To use another seed, set `SEED` to a whole number from 0 to 4294967295. A failing random test prints the seed it used.

macOS or Linux:

```bash
SEED=12345 npm test
```

Windows Command Prompt:

```bat
set SEED=12345
npm test
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:SEED = "12345"
npm test
```

In Command Prompt and PowerShell the variable stays set in that window. Clear it with `set SEED=` or `Remove-Item Env:SEED`.

### Commands that were run

On macOS 15.7.5 (zsh) on 2026-10-23, with Node v24.21.0 and npm 11.19.0:

## Testing

The 125 tests are in six files and run with `npm test`. Nothing needs installing.

- **Unit tests for each acceptance criterion** (`tests/stories.test.js`, `tests/edge-cases.test.js`). Test names start with the criterion id, such as `S-3.1`.
- **Invariant tests with seeded random cases** (`tests/invariants.test.js`). For example, the shares always add up exactly to the total and differ by at most 1 cent.
- **Message tests** (`tests/messages.test.js`). One for every message the page can show.
- **Docs-sync tests**, DOCS-1 to DOCS-12 (`tests/docs.test.js`). They fail if the docs and the code drift apart: every message is quoted in the stories doc and the other way round, every criterion has a test or is on the list checked by hand or on the not-built list, the limits match, and each story status matches the test report.
- **PAGE- tests**, PAGE-1 to PAGE-16 (`tests/page.test.js`). PAGE-1 to PAGE-8 read `index.html`, `styles.css` and `app.js` as text. PAGE-9 to PAGE-16 run `app.js` against a small stand-in for the page.

To check that the tests can fail, bugs were planted one at a time in throwaway copies outside the project, for example rounding the tip down instead of half-up, or giving the extra cents to the last people. Where a planted bug was not caught, a test was added until it was.

**Only checked by hand.** The automated tests never load the page in a browser. Eleven criteria depend on the page itself, so they count as passed only because I checked them by hand in Chrome and Safari: S-1.1 (the first open), S-4.15 (a message sits under its entry), S-5.1 to S-5.6 (the amounts follow every change) and S-6.1 to S-6.3 (Reset). A few other checks, such as the 320 px width and keyboard-only use, were not recorded, so they are not confirmed.

The results for every criterion, and what is not covered, are in [docs/test-report.md](docs/test-report.md).

## Assumptions

- **The number of people includes the payer**, who also owes a share. The page does not say so.
- **The bill is the amount on the check**, with any tax or service charge already in it. The tip is added on top. There is no separate tax entry.
- **The tip is worked out on the bill as entered**: the percentage times the bill, rounded half-up to the cent, once. The total is the bill plus the tip. For example, a bill of 1.05 at 10% is 0.105, which shows as 0.11. A calculator that uses floating point can show 0.10. The page does not say it rounds half-up.
- **Equal split only.** When the total does not divide evenly, the leftover cents go one each to the first people, meaning the first places in the numbered list. People are not named, so who gets the extra cent does not matter. The result says so, and the shares add up exactly to the total.
- **Currency-neutral display.** Amounts have two decimals, with no currency symbol and no thousands separators, so what you read is what you can type, for example `2000000.00`. This assumes a currency with two decimal places.
- **Limits.** Bill 0.01 to 1000000.00. Tip 0 to 100, with up to two decimals. People 1 to 50, as a whole number. Anything else gets a message and no result. A bill of 0.01 split three ways is allowed and shows 0.01, 0.00 and 0.00.
- **Input rules.**
  - Bill and Tip %: digits and at most one decimal point, up to two decimals. ".5" and "5." are fine. "." on its own is not.
  - People: digits only, so "2.5", "2.0" and "2." are rejected.
  - Leading zeros are fine: "007" is 7.
  - Spaces, tabs and non-breaking spaces at the ends are ignored. Other blank characters, and any blank inside a number, are rejected.
  - Commas, signs, exponents, letters and digits from other scripts are rejected.
  - Only a decimal point is accepted as the decimal mark. I have not checked whether a phone keypad in a region that uses a comma offers a point.
  - If a value has too many decimals and is also out of range, the message about decimals is shown.
  - An empty Bill is not an error: there is just no result yet. An empty Tip % or People gets its own message.
- **Messages follow every keystroke**, so a message can show briefly while a number is half typed. For example, typing 0 on the way to 0.50 shows "The bill must be at least 0.01." until the next digit.
- **English only.** The page stores nothing and sends nothing.
